story_villain_track/stage_proving_yard.alt: The Proving Yard: A sand training ground ringed by stands, with a scoreboard that shows the hero programme ranking in real time.

story_villain_track/stage_harbour_front.alt: The Harbour Front: Corvane’s waterfront: fish stalls by day, and this week a festival stage going up on the main pier, strings of paper lanterns, broadcast vans.

story_villain_track/stage_registry.alt: The Registry: The academy archive under the admin tower: forty years of files on every graduate, in grey steel drawers that open only to a licence badge.

story_villain_track/stage_old_bridge.alt: The Old Bridge: A stone bridge over the harbour mouth, closed to traffic.

story_villain_track/celeste.alt: Celeste Moreau, Top-ranked final-year on the hero programme, holder of the First Badge, and the person you were sent to rob

story_villain_track/stage_waterline_prec.alt: Waterline Precinct: The harbour district police station: a front desk, a vending machine that steals coins, framed newspaper front pages of academy heroes thanking the police.

story_villain_track/marrow.alt: Dean Marrow, Masked Dean of Applied Opposition, the course with no room number, and the man who put the black mask in your hand

story_villain_track/cover.alt: Cover art for Villain Track: Hero academy. You’re on the villain track.

story_villain_track/juno.alt: Juno Pike, Final-year on the villain track, your handler, and in daylight the resident advisor of your dorm

story_villain_track/tolle.alt: Bram Tolle, Ungifted officer at Waterline Precinct, working the masquerade’s security cordon because he asked to

story_villain_track/dray.alt: Professor Anselm Dray, Head of the Hero Programme, the city’s most famous living hero, and the bronze statue in the middle of the Quad

story_villain_track/rafe.alt: Rafe Corrigan, Another first-year with a black mask in his pocket, and the same assignment as you

story_rank_zero/stage_medical_wing.alt: The Medical Wing: Eight treatment bays with green curtains, a smell of antiseptic and instant noodles, and a whiteboard of who is on shift.

story_rank_zero/stage_atrium.alt: The Atrium: A glass-roofed atrium at the centre of the academy, and the Board: a wall of two hundred and forty names in order, updating live.

story_rank_zero/stage_rating_office.alt: The Rating Office: A low concrete room under the Intake Hall, full of humming cabinets, cable trays and a bench rig that is a small copy of the Gauge.

story_nova_house/stage_ruth_study.alt: Ruth’s Study: A small room off the kitchen with an armchair Ruth sleeps in more often than her bed, a desk of college paperwork, a framed police commendation turned to face the wall, and a bottom drawer that sticks.

story_nova_house/stage_the_hall.alt: The Front Hall: Coat hooks, muddy boots, the stairs, and a chalkboard of house rules in four handwritings: 1.

story_rank_zero/stage_intake_hall.alt: The Intake Hall: A high white hall with a viewing gallery, two hundred and forty cadets in lines, and the Gauge at the far end: a glass column taller than a person with a brass hand plate, now black to the ceiling and dripping extinguisher foam.

story_nova_house/stage_the_dining_room.alt: The Dining Room: A long scrubbed table with five mismatched chairs, a hatch through to the kitchen, and a window onto the orchard.

story_nova_house/stage_the_kitchen.alt: Ruth’s Kitchen: Ruth’s territory: a range that is never off, a washing-up rota in four handwritings, a radio turned low, and a locked steel tin on the top shelf that nobody is supposed to mention.

story_nova_house/stage_the_parlour.alt: The Parlour: The good room, used once a year.

story_rank_zero/stage_sealed_wing.alt: The Old Hall: The sealed east wing: the academy’s first intake hall, closed nineteen years ago.

story_rank_zero/stage_the_dorms.alt: The Cadet Dorms: Three blocks around a courtyard.

story_rank_zero/stage_mess_hall.alt: The Mess: Long tables in track order, Field by the windows and Reserve by the kitchen.

story_nova_house/stage_the_landing.alt: The Landing: Four doors and a creaking floor.

story_rank_zero/stage_the_bowl.alt: The Bowl: A sunken sand arena with stone stands, four sparring rings chalked on the floor, racks of training staves and weighted balls.

story_nova_house/stage_room_four.alt: Room Four: Your room, and Corin Abbott’s until April.

story_nova_house/stage_lena_room.alt: Lena’s Room: Every wall papered with charcoal frames of things that have not happened yet, dated in the corner.

story_nova_house/stage_haru_room.alt: Haru’s Room: Tiled floor to ceiling like a kitchen, a metal bed, scorch marks on the ceiling in the shape of bad nights, a window that is always open, and a packed bag under the bed that he has not unpacked since his second fire.

story_rank_zero/stage_director_tower.alt: The Director’s Office: The top floor of the old lighthouse tower.

story_nova_house/stage_sable_room.alt: Sable’s Room: Bare and tidy: a made bed, one chair, a grey coat on the back of the door, and nothing on the walls at all.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_carc.alt: The Carcass Yard: A walled yard behind the hall with a weighing beam, meat hooks, a drain, a shed where Harl Benning sleeps, and a cart gate whose lock has not worked since spring.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_orsk.alt: The Guildmaster’s Loft: Up the back stairs: one long room under the roof, full of old maps of the ridges pinned over each other, a cold iron stove, a chair the guildmaster sleeps in, and a locked chest he keeps his boots on.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_ford.alt: Ford Square: Cobbles, a market, a smithy ringing, and the stone bridge over the ford that gives the town its name.

story_rank_zero/stage_ferry_pier.alt: The Ferry Pier: A wooden pier, a ticket hut, and the squat green ferry that crosses to the harbour every forty minutes.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_guil.alt: The Guild Hall: The biggest building in Kestrel Ford: a long timber hall with a counter at one end, the guild crystal on a stand beside it, a notice board, a B-rank table by the fire that everyone else steps around, and five enormous wyvern skulls hung from the rafters, older than anybody drinking under them.

story_rank_zero/stage_harbour_town.alt: Calder Bay Harbour: The mainland waterfront: noodle counters, a hero-merch shop selling the top ten cadets’ faces on mugs, and the glass offices of the agencies that sponsor them.

story_nova_house/stage_attunement_rooms.alt: The Attunement Rooms: Where abilities are trained: padded rooms with observation windows, fireproof benches for the pyrokinetics, a silent room for the readers, and instructors with clipboards.

story_nova_house/stage_halloran_green.alt: Halloran Green: The college’s main lawn, ringed by the big houses with their lit windows and their noise.

story_nova_house/stage_the_dome.alt: The Dome: The old observatory on the roof that gave the house its name: a brass telescope on an iron mount, a slit in the dome that still opens, two folding chairs, and the whole college laid out below.

story_rank_zero/valk.alt: Ines Valk, Combat instructor for the first years, ex-field hero, and the only person who walked into the smoke

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/key.alt: Key art for Level One, Wyvern Slayer

story_rank_zero/stage_the_seawall.alt: The Seawall: A long stone wall along the north shore, wide enough to sit on, with the lights of the harbour across the water.

story_rank_zero/cover.alt: Cover art for Rank Zero: It read zero. Then it caught fire.

story_rank_zero/riku.alt: Riku Amano, Number one on the Board, rated 9,412, sponsored by an agency since the day he turned eighteen

story_nova_house/stage_the_orchard.alt: The Orchard: Old apple trees behind the house, long grass, and a brick wall at the bottom that is scorched black in a man-sized patch where Haru burns off the day.

story_nova_house/stage_provost_tower.alt: The Provost’s Tower: The Provost’s office at the top of the old library tower, with his rooms above it: a fire always lit, deep chairs, a pot of tea going cold, a window over the whole green, and a desk drawer that is locked when he is out.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_back_corr.alt: The Back Corridors: Narrow service passages behind the dungeon’s walls, lit by grubby lamps, where goblin staff push trolleys of fresh coins, reset spring traps and complain.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_ninth_vau.alt: The Ninth Vault: The deepest room in the Gilt Deep.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_hall_of_f.alt: The Hall of False Chests: A long hall above the vault with forty chests in four rows, every one of them identical to you from the outside and every one of them empty, trapped, or both.

story_the_last_mimic/key.alt: Key art for The Last Mimic

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_spli.alt: The Split Tankard: The adventurers’ inn on the square: low beams, a long bar, the ranked parties’ tables by the fire and everybody else by the door.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_keepers_s.alt: The Keeper’s Study: A dry, warm, beautifully kept office one floor up from the vault.

story_nova_house/stage_the_quiet_wing.alt: The Quiet Wing: A basement corridor under the infirmary, behind a door with no sign: four clean rooms with soft chairs, a dispensary cabinet of Stillwater, and a chair by each bed for somebody to sit in.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_apot.alt: The Apothecary Attic: Fia Quenby’s room above the apothecary: a slanted ceiling, a narrow bed, and every wall covered in chalk charts of crystal readings, kills and wound angles.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_asce.alt: The Ascent House: A narrow grey townhouse with velvet curtains and a brass plate.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_old_.alt: The Old Watch: A squat stone tower at the town’s east edge, built by the guild’s founders to watch the ridges for wyverns.

story_rank_zero/sana.alt: Sana Tsuda, First-year medic cadet, rank 74 on the Support track, rated first thing and put straight on the medic station, so she was beside the Gauge when it burned

story_nova_house/stage_the_glasshouse.alt: The Glasshouse: A long Victorian glasshouse at the edge of the green, warm and wet and green, where the college grows tomatoes and lemons and things for the infirmary.

story_nova_house/stage_lowbridge.alt: Lowbridge: The river town at the bottom of the hill: a stone bridge, a café that stays open late for students, a bus stop with one timetable on it, and lanterns strung along the river for Founders’ Night.

story_rank_zero/hale.alt: Okon Hale, Director of Lodestar Academy for fourteen years, former licensed hero, and the man with a statement for you to sign

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_east.alt: The East Road: The cart road out of town toward the ridges, between hedges and the open ford meadow where the town’s cattle graze.

story_rank_zero/ada.alt: Ada Kole, The ferry’s engineer, who rarely comes up the ladder

story_rank_zero/halvorsen.alt: Noor Halvorsen, The Ratings Bureau’s resident technician at Lodestar, and the engineer who built the Gauge

story_nova_house/lena.alt: Lena Morrow, Precog, second-year, who draws the future in still frames and already drew you

story_rank_zero/calla.alt: Calla Reyes, Rank 239, your neighbour across the Reserve corridor, re-sitting her first year

story_nova_house/haru.alt: Haru Ezaki, Pyrokinetic, third-year, with two fires on his record and the loudest mind in the house

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_staff_can.alt: The Staff Canteen: Where the Deep’s staff eat: three long tables, a stew pot as big as a delver, a rota on the wall and a noticeboard of grievances.

story_nova_house/cover.alt: Cover art for Nova House: You read minds. One of them plans murder.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_long_stai.alt: The Long Stair: Nine floors of switchback stair from the vault to the surface, with a landing on every floor and a trap on most.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_gallery_o.alt: The Gallery of Echoes: The oldest room in the Deep: a curved gallery of pale stone that keeps every voice ever spoken in it and plays them back, softly and out of order, for ever.

story_nova_house/sorrell.alt: Nathaniel Sorrell, Provost of Halloran College. A gentle man with a voice that makes you agree

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_the_.alt: The Nest: A flat crag above the second scree, wind-scoured, littered with old bones and broken shell, with the whole valley and the town spread out below.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_delvers_c.alt: The Delvers’ Camp: A safe landing on the third floor where the Guild’s rules say nobody fights: braziers, bedrolls, a Guild noticeboard, and a man selling bad tea at good prices.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/stage_scal.alt: Scald Ridge: Burnt pines, loose scree and a long black scorch where the wyvern came down on you last night.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/gale.alt: Gale Marrick, Leader of the Ninefold, the best B-rank party in the hall, level thirty-eight, and the first person to put a price on you

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_well_mout.alt: The Well Mouth: Where the Gilt Deep meets the town: a wide stone well with a stair spiralling down its inside, a Guild checkpoint with a ledger and two bored guards, and Brightwell’s market crowding right up to the rim.

story_nova_house/ruth.alt: Ruth Calder, House Mother of Nova House. Former police empath, current keeper of the keys and the soup

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/fia.alt: Fia Quenby, A mage at level thirty-one on paper, dropped from Gale’s party a month ago, and the only person in the hall measuring the wound instead of laughing

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/tamsin.alt: Tamsin Wick, The guild receptionist. She runs the counter, the crystal and the day book, and she has just read your number aloud to the whole hall

story_nova_house/corin.alt: Corin Abbott, Gardener at the college glasshouse, who keeps stopping at the Nova House gate

story_nova_house/sable.alt: Sable Quint, Fourth-year whose mind is silent, and within arm’s reach of whom every ability stops

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_guildhous.alt: The Guildhouse: The Delvers’ Guild hall on the square: a contract board, a counting room, a bounty wall, and up in the tower a great bronze chime that had not rung in thirty years until tonight.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_stitchers.alt: The Stitchers’ Hall: A long workshop where deep satchels are made and mended: shelves of bags that used to hold a wagonload each and now hold a week’s shopping.

story_the_last_mimic/stage_the_first_vau.alt: The First Vault: A vault under the vault, on no map and at the bottom of no stair: a perfectly round room with a ring of old iron bands set into the floor, where the first mimic in the Deep woke up.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/harl.alt: Harl Benning, Keeper of the carcass yard behind the hall, on a cane, and the porter Gale’s party left on the ridge eight days ago

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/orsk.alt: Hadric Orsk, Guildmaster of Kestrel Ford, a former wyvern hand with a ruined knee, who has not come down the back stairs for a new member in eleven years

story_the_last_mimic/lirelle.alt: Lirelle, Elf thief with her hand in your coins. Licensed delver, and in debt to the Guild for more than she will ever see

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/cover.alt: Cover art for Level One, Wyvern Slayer: Level one on paper. Wyvern on the floor.

story_the_last_mimic/ash.alt: Ash, The lich who keeps the Gilt Deep. Dead for three hundred and twelve years, and still doing the accounts

story_the_last_mimic/cover.alt: Cover art for The Last Mimic: Reborn as a treasure chest. With teeth.

story_level_one_wyvern_slayer/marguerite.alt: Marguerite Sallow, Broker at the Ascent House, which arranges escorted kills for rich families and sells the draw that comes with them

story_the_last_mimic/pell.alt: Pell, Goblin on the Deep’s staff. Polishes the treasure, restocks the chests, and has talked to you twice a day for six months

story_echo_class/stage_the_dorms.alt: The Residence Block: Two wings of student rooms joined by a shared kitchen that always smells of instant noodles and toast.

story_the_last_mimic/edda.alt: Edda Quell, The Delvers’ Guild’s senior appraiser. Carries the silver chime that rings near a mimic, and has come to collect you

story_the_last_mimic/bruno.alt: Bruno Fenn, Lirelle’s shield-bearer. A big, careful man on what he has promised is his last delve

story_echo_class/stage_great_hall.alt: The Great Hall: A long stone hall with a vaulted ceiling, two hundred chairs and a stage.

story_echo_class/stage_the_quad.alt: The Quad: A wide paved square between the Great Hall, the Residence Block and the Pit, with a dry fountain in the middle that the Back Row sits on at lunch.

story_echo_class/stage_room_4c.alt: Room 4C: Two beds, two desks and a window that sticks.

story_echo_class/stage_the_pit.alt: The Pit: A sunken arena, sand over rubber, ringed by six tiers of benches.

story_echo_class/stage_gym_roof.alt: The Gym Roof: A flat gravel roof above the Pit with a rail, a water tank and the whole harbour below.

story_echo_class/stage_infirmary.alt: The Infirmary: Six beds, blackout curtains, and a nurse who has seen every kind of drop and is not impressed by yours.

story_echo_class/stage_adair_lab.alt: Adair’s Lab: The Power Theory lab: measuring rigs bolted to the floor, a slow-motion camera on a track, and a wall clock with a second hand loud enough to hear from the corridor.

story_echo_class/stage_records_room.alt: Records Room 0: A cold basement of grey cabinets that the Registry rents from the academy and never visits.

story_echo_class/stage_registry_annex.alt: The Registry Annex: A borrowed office with a borrowed desk, two chairs and a window onto the quad.

story_echo_class/stage_velling_harbour.alt: Velling Harbour: The town below the academy: ferries, a fish market, a noodle shop open until two, and the rebuilt pier with a bronze plaque listing the sixty-one people who walked off it.

story_echo_class/stage_boathouse.alt: The Boathouse: An old timber boathouse on the shore below the hill, rowing shells racked on the walls and a chalk ring on the floor where off-the-books fights happen.

story_echo_class/yuna.alt: Yuna Takeda, Second-year ranked first of twelve hundred. Gravity, and the hand you just shook

story_echo_class/teo.alt: Teo Vance, Your roommate in 4C. Ranked three hundred and eighty-eighth; hears electricity, sells noodles and odds

story_echo_class/rook.alt: Callum Rook, Third-year ranked ninth. Head of the Back Row, and the first person to make you an offer

story_echo_class/adair.alt: Professor Imogen Adair, Head of Power Theory and combat fundamentals. Was going to be one of the best heroes in the country, until something ended it in her fourth year

story_echo_class/cover.alt: Cover art for Echo Class: Copy any power you touch. Sixty seconds.

story_echo_class/marsh.alt: Delphine Marsh, Classification officer for the national Registry, with one file in her case. Yours

story_rescue_rating/stage_rooftop_line.alt: The Rooftop Line: A path across the flat roofs of the old warehouse district: planks over the gaps, ladders bolted to chimneys, a kettle somebody leaves on a ledge.

story_rescue_rating/stage_the_underline.alt: The Underline: A loop of subway tunnel closed sixty years ago, under the old docks.

story_rescue_rating/stage_harbour_front.alt: Harbour Front: Six lanes of waterfront, food trucks, a ferry terminal, and a giant screen on the terminal wall that shows the Ladder’s top ten all night.

story_rescue_rating/stage_the_rooftop.alt: Pier Tower Roof: The flat top of an unfinished forty-storey tower over the harbour: rebar, tarps, wet concrete and a construction crane with its arm snapped and hanging.

story_rescue_rating/stage_the_switchyard.alt: The Switchyard: An old signal room at the heart of the Underline: a wall of dead switches, a kettle on a camping stove, a mattress, and a cork board covered in Tallyhouse floor plans and photographs of a collapsed car park.

story_rescue_rating/stage_bureau_office.alt: Bureau Harbour Office: The Rescue Bureau’s harbour office: a front desk, four holding rooms, and a night dispatch floor where Kit Navarro watches thirty-eight rookie streams on six screens.

story_rescue_rating/stage_your_flat.alt: Your Flat: One room on the nineteenth floor of Stack Fourteen: a bed, a hot plate, a window over the harbour, your spare uniform drying on a chair, and a cork board of call logs from three months of mostly getting cats out of things.

story_rescue_rating/stage_the_stacks.alt: The Stacks: Twenty residential towers on the hill above the harbour, joined by walkways, with a night market on the bottom four floors.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_sh.alt: The Shrine Courtyard: Raked gravel at the top of three hundred and four steps, ringed by cedar.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_st.alt: The Storehouse: A white-walled storehouse with a door you have to lift as you unlock it.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_ma.alt: The Main Hall: A dark wooden hall whose roof leaks onto the altar when it rains.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_ke.alt: The Keeper’s House: Two rooms and a kitchen beside the hall.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/key.alt: Key art for Married to the Shrine Fox

story_rescue_rating/stage_tallyhouse_tow.alt: Tallyhouse Tower: A glass tower on Glasshill with the Feed’s logo turning on the roof.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_c.alt: The Calling Hall: A round stone hall with tall windows, a gallery, and a dais for the staff.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_t.alt: The Refectory: Long tables by year, a high table for the staff under a window of green glass, and four hundred witches at supper.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_r.alt: Room Nine, North Tower: A tower room with two narrow beds, two desks, one window over the grey estuary, and a curtain on a rope down the exact middle.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_t.alt: The Cloister: A covered stone walk round a square courtyard with a well in the middle, and the way to everything inside the Hedge.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/key.alt: Key art for The Only Man at Thornwitch

story_rescue_rating/stage_counting_floor.alt: The Counting Floor: Tallyhouse’s sixty-first floor: no windows, three hundred screens, and twelve people in headsets watching every live rescue in the city.

story_rescue_rating/stage_studio_nine.alt: Studio Nine: The Feed’s live studio: a white sofa, three cameras, a wall-sized screen of the Ladder, and a green room with free food, sponsor contracts laid out on the table and spare staff lanyards hanging on hooks by the door.

story_rescue_rating/stage_calder_span.alt: The Calder Span: The great suspension bridge across the bay: two white towers and six lanes.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_no.alt: The Old Wall: Behind the hall the mountain drops steeply, held back by a dry stone wall laid by hand three hundred years ago, a fox carved on every seventh stone.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_ce.alt: The Great Cedar: A cedar older than the shrine, roped with thick straw and white paper zigzags, its roots split into a hollow big enough for a fox to sleep in.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_th.alt: The Three Hundred Steps: Three hundred and four mossy stone steps down through cedar, a red gate at the top, the middle and the bottom, and a stone lantern every twenty steps.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_su.alt: Sugino Main Street: The town’s one street: a post office, the town office, a shuttered bakery with Sora’s flat above it, a bathhouse with a painted mountain on the wall, and ropeway posters on every pole, half of them torn down and half of them put back.

story_rescue_rating/sloane.alt: Sloane Lyle, The most wanted woman in Calder Bay, whom no camera has ever seen, currently in your arms

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_l.alt: The Long Library: A gallery a hundred yards long, books chained to the shelves, window seats over the estuary, and the Founders’ Charter under glass at the far end.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_t.alt: The Rookery: The headmistress’s study at the top of the oldest tower: a desk, three hundred years of portraits, a window on every side, a brass lamp with no wick, and a tall wooden perch by the desk with nothing on it.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_um.alt: Kanzaki General Store: Rice balls at four, batteries, rubber boots, a chest freezer that hums, and a bench outside where the town decides things before the meeting does.

story_rescue_rating/dante.alt: Dante Roe, Number one on the Ladder for four years, and the hero this crane was booked for

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_d.alt: The Deputy’s Office: Net curtains, a biscuit tin, a wall of labelled box files, and a ring of brass keys on a hook by the door.

story_rescue_rating/kit.alt: Kit Navarro, Your handler on the Bureau’s night desk, and the voice in your earpiece

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_t.alt: The Kitchens: Copper pans, a range the size of a cart, steam, islander cooks who do not care who you are, and a long black cat on the warm end of the range who cares a great deal.

story_rescue_rating/cover.alt: Cover art for Rescue Rating: You saved the city’s most wanted. Live.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_t.alt: The Bowl: A sunken lawn ringed by a grass bank, where students practise and duel inside chalk circles.

story_rescue_rating/vask.alt: Corinne Vask, Tallyhouse’s Head of Live Events, who schedules the city’s accidents

story_rescue_rating/mensah.alt: Tobiah Mensah, Sergeant in Bureau Enforcement, the sirens coming up the tower, with a warrant for Sloane Lyle

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_mi.alt: The Mist Bridge: A rope-and-plank bridge over a gorge that fills with mist even at noon, reached from behind the great cedar once the mist has come up the mountain.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/kuzuha.alt: Kuzuha, The nine-tailed fox of the mountain, who says your family owes her a wedding

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/sora.alt: Sora Yanagi, Shrine maiden. Has kept the shrine running alone since the last keeper died

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_g.alt: The Grey Reach: The north end of the island, where the Hedge has gone the colour of ash for a hundred yards.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_bu.alt: The Bus Stop: A tin shelter at the end of the street with a timetable nobody needs to read: the last bus down the valley leaves at 19:52.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/stage_th.alt: The Kawase Inn: An old wooden inn with eleven rooms and two guests.

story_rescue_rating/chat.alt: The Chat, Forty thousand strangers watching your shoulder camera, all typing at once

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_c.alt: The Chamber of Seven Chairs: A panelled room with seven tall chairs in a half-circle, a public gallery above, and an archive cabinet nobody has opened in a long time.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/cover.alt: Cover art for Married to the Shrine Fox: Your family owes a fox a wedding.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_f.alt: The Founders’ Garden: A walled clearing inside the roots of the Hedge, reached only through a door the Hedge grew over three hundred years ago.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_h.alt: The Hedge Gate: The only gap in the Hedge: an arch of living thorn twelve feet high that opens for the people it chooses, and the start of the stone causeway across the mud to the mainland.
The Hedge Walk: A gravel path between the college buildings and the Hedge itself, which goes up forty feet like a black wall and ticks and creaks in the wind.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/oboro.alt: Oboro, Yokai of the valley mist, who offers to make the vow go away for free

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/ume.alt: Ume Kanzaki, Runs the general store, and has fed every keeper of the shrine for sixty years

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/stage_f.alt: Fenn’s Landing: A wooden jetty below the causeway, a tarred ferry, and a hut with a stove pipe where Tobias Fenn has lived his whole life outside the Hedge.

story_married_to_the_shrine_fox/tadokoro.alt: Isao Tadokoro, Property developer from the town, buying the mountain for a ropeway and a hot-spring hotel

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/ivy.alt: Ivy Calder, First of the fourth year, and the headmistress’s chosen apprentice

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/cover.alt: Cover art for The Only Man at Thornwitch: Her raven chose you. Explain yourself.

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/nadia.alt: Nadia Kowal, Second-year herb witch on a scholarship, and the other half of Room Nine

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/morgain.alt: Morgaine Ashdown, Headmistress of Thornwitch for twenty-one years, and until this morning the raven’s

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/sexton.alt: Sexton, The headmistress’s raven for three centuries, and since this morning yours

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/cass.alt: Cass, The last headmistress’s cat, who runs the kitchens’ trade in secrets

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/hester.alt: Hester Crane, Deputy Head and Mistress of Discipline, who has wanted the headmistress’s chair for nine years

story_the_only_man_at_thornwitch/tobias.alt: Tobias Fenn, The ferryman outside the Hedge, and the only other man on the island

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_guest_roo.alt: The Guest Rooms: A corridor of seven doors.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_inn_cella.alt: The Cellar: Stone steps down to barrels gone dry, a wine rack with three bottles nobody can identify, a crate of old guest books, and a low door behind the racks into a second, smaller cellar no plan of the house shows.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_common_ro.alt: The Common Room: Long, low and smelling of wet ash.

story_the_one_copper_inn/key.alt: Key art for The One-Copper Inn

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_inn_kitch.alt: The Kitchen: A black iron range the size of a cart that has not been lit in twenty years, copper pans gone green on their hooks, a scrubbed table, and a back door that opens onto Old Marla’s vegetable patch.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_stable_ya.alt: The Stable Yard: A cobbled yard and a stable with the only sound roof on the property, because Tobin re-slated it himself.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_mechanics_bu.alt: The Bunkhouse: Twelve bunks in a prefab behind the main hangar, a kettle that trips the fuse, a dartboard with a cadet’s photo pinned to it, and a shift roster on the door.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_marlas_co.alt: Old Marla’s Cottage: A whitewashed cottage over the low wall, with four beehives, a goat called The Bishop tethered to the gate, a kitchen that smells permanently of onions and bread, and a dented biscuit tin on the top shelf that Marla moves out of reach whenever anybody looks at it.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_hangar_nine.alt: Hangar Nine: The last hangar on the row, half-lit, where suits wait for the breakers.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_the_crag.alt: The Crag: A shoulder of grey rock above the inn where something heavy came down last night.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_north_roa.alt: The North Road: The old coaching road, grass growing up its middle, climbing past the inn toward the mountains.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_main_hangar.alt: The Main Hangar: Six working gantries with cadet suits in for service, the smell of hydraulic fluid and burnt coffee, and a radio nobody admits to owning.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_the_mess.alt: The Mess Hall: Long tables for two hundred cadets, with the hangar crews at the end table by the bins.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_hunters_c.alt: The Hunters’ Camp: Six canvas tents around the old shrine at the crossroads, a picket line of good horses, racks of chain-bolt crossbows under oilcloth, and a long cookfire where twenty hunters eat in shifts.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_ford_mark.alt: Brindle Ford Market: A market square on the river with a stone cross in the middle, a baker, a chandler, a smith, and the Drowned Ox, the only tavern, whose landlord would like you to fail.

story_the_one_copper_inn/stage_reeves_ha.alt: The Reeve’s Hall: A narrow stone toll house on the bridge.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_cadet_quarte.alt: The Cadet Block: Three storeys of cadet rooms with a duty desk at the door that checks passes after ten.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_the_pit.alt: The Pit: A sparring bowl cut into the cliff and ringed with stepped concrete seats, where cadets fight bouts in suits with blunted blades and the results go straight to the Board.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_the_seawall.alt: The Seawall: A kilometre of concrete between the town and the open sea, with gun posts every hundred metres and suit bays dug into its back.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_command_towe.alt: The Command Tower: Glass at the top where the Commandant works, records at the bottom, and a lift that takes forty seconds and tells everybody in the lobby who is going up.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_breakers_yar.alt: The Breakers’ Yard: A concrete apron at the foot of the cliff where retired suits are cut for scrap: a cutting rig on rails, a crane, a heap of armour plate rusting in the spray.

story_the_one_copper_inn/ember.alt: Ember, Your first guest. A red dragon in human shape, wounded, with hunters a mile behind her

story_the_one_copper_inn/wren.alt: Captain Corin Wren, Captain of the Greyhook Company, twenty dragon hunters under crown warrant. Polite, patient, and at your door

story_the_one_copper_inn/cover.alt: Cover art for The One-Copper Inn: Your first guest is a dragon.

story_the_one_copper_inn/marla.alt: Old Marla, Your only neighbour. Cooked at this inn for thirty years, and has opinions about your range

story_the_one_copper_inn/tobin.alt: Tobin Ashby, Stablehand who came with the inn. Nobody told him to stop, so he kept working

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_gullwater.alt: Gullwater: The harbour town under the headland: a fish market, two bars, a noodle stall run by Tova’s mother, and four thousand people who live behind the Seawall and know exactly what the academy is for.

story_ironclad_cadets/stage_hollow_coast.alt: The Hollow Coast: Forty minutes north of the Seawall at a suit’s walking pace: a grey shore of collapsed bunkers and the rusted shells of derelicts that never finished walking, some of them still twitching.

story_ironclad_cadets/tova.alt: Tova Brask, Your bunkmate on the night shift, and the loudest mechanic in the hangar

story_ironclad_cadets/haldor.alt: Haldor Quist, Second on the Board, heir to the foundry that built Unit Nine, and the cadet who will make sure you know your place

story_ironclad_cadets/kaede.alt: Kaede Strand, Cadet lieutenant, first on the Board, and the pilot who tried to wake Unit Nine forty-one times

story_the_one_copper_inn/thatch.alt: Reeve Imogen Thatch, Reeve of Brindle Ford. Keeps the town’s ledgers, sold you the inn, and will decide whether it counts as one

story_crest_academy/stage_great_hall.alt: The Great Hall: A long hall of dark beams and banners where four hundred students eat seated by rank: nobles at the high tables, the scholar at the last seat by the door.

story_ironclad_cadets/graf.alt: Ilse Graf, Commandant of the academy, who signed the order to cut Unit Nine

story_ironclad_cadets/ruiz.alt: Bo Ruiz, Chief of the hangar, your boss, and the man who put you on Unit Nine on purpose

story_crest_academy/stage_the_ring.alt: The Ring: A circle of raked white sand ringed by waist-high stone rails, with the Rail Room’s windows above one side and the royal box under a green awning on the other.

story_crest_academy/stage_rail_room.alt: The Rail Room: The Rail Society’s lounge, up a stair above the Ring: leather chairs, decanters, a long window over the sand, and a burgundy ledger open on a lectern.

story_ironclad_cadets/pip.alt: Pip, Unit Nine’s onboard intelligence: twenty-three years in service, eleven of them silent. Wherever the suit is, Pip is

story_crest_academy/stage_training_yard.alt: The Training Yard: A walled yard of packed earth, wooden pells and straw targets scorched by a thousand first-year spells.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_ring_hall.alt: The Ring Hall: A round chamber under the cathedral dome, cold as a well.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_cathedral_n.alt: The Cathedral Nave: The long body of the cathedral: four hundred candles, pilgrims in grey cloaks packed shoulder to shoulder, the Circle Guard in white at every pillar, and a gilded dais where the hero will take his oath at five.

story_the_hero_s_spare/key.alt: Key art for The Hero’s Spare

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_warden_cell.alt: The Warden Cells: Nine cells cut into the rock under the cathedral, dry and swept, with a cot, a blanket and a slot in each door.

story_ironclad_cadets/cover.alt: Cover art for Unit Nine: Scrap at six. It asked you to stay.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_wardens_yar.alt: The Wardens’ Yard: A walled drill yard behind the cathedral where the Circle Wardens train, eat and sleep in a long barracks.

story_crest_academy/stage_east_tower.alt: The East Tower: The noble dormitory, five floors of panelled rooms around a spiral stair.

story_crest_academy/stage_founders_hall.alt: Founders’ Hall: The council chamber: twelve high-backed chairs for the governors, the Headmistress’s seal on a stand, and the Scholars’ Board on the wall under a cloth, twenty-eight names long.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_moot_.alt: The Moot Hall: The town’s hall of business: a long room with the evidence table laid out for the assize, the strongroom door with its smashed lock, the reeve’s desk and ledgers, and on the far wall, under glass gone black with a century of soot, the Hill Charter.

story_crest_academy/stage_gatehouse_room.alt: The Gatehouse Room: Your room: the old porter’s room over the gate arch, with the portcullis winch in one corner, a narrow bed, and a window onto the cliff stairs.

story_crest_academy/stage_library.alt: The Library: Three floors of shelves around a well of light.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_ford_.alt: Ford Square: The cobbled heart of Kettlecross: a gallows used twice a decade, a trestle table where the circuit holds its dawn assize, the town well, and a bell tower that has leaned since the dragon sat on it sixty-one years ago.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_c.alt: The Crooked Kettle: The only inn in Kettlecross, with a common room of six tables and a hearth, a loft where the stranger has slept on credit for eight nights, and a slate behind the bar with the stranger’s debt chalked on it in Ysolde’s square hand.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_bell_tower.alt: The Bell Tower: Two hundred and twelve steps up from the nave, three of which creak.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_archive.alt: The Archive: Six floors of shelves around a shaft of light, connected by ladders on rails, smelling of dust and lamp oil.

story_crest_academy/stage_below_stairs.alt: Below Stairs: Kitchens, laundries and the maid-knights’ dormitory under the Great Hall, hot, loud and run like a ship.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_kettl.alt: The Kettle Kitchen: Ysolde’s kitchen: a range that runs hot on the left, a larder with a whole ham, river eels, onions older than the stranger, flour, eggs and a crock of good butter, and a grease-stained book on the top shelf that nobody has opened in years.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_long_galler.alt: The Long Gallery: The palace’s great gallery, where the regent holds standing court because there are no chairs.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_hero_rooms.alt: The Hero’s Rooms: Three gilded rooms off a guarded corridor, built for heroes and used once a generation: a bed the size of a hay cart, a bath nobody has filled, a table of food Kai has not touched, and a portrait of the ninth hero turned to face the wall.

story_three_skills_a_morning/key.alt: Key art for Three Skills a Morning

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_lantern_mar.alt: Lantern Market: The square in front of the cathedral and the streets that run off it: paper lanterns strung between houses, a honey-bun stall, a pilgrims’ cloak seller, a notice board with the church’s seal on every sheet, and a crowd that has already heard there were two.

story_crest_academy/stage_infirmary.alt: The Infirmary: Twelve white beds, a healer with no patience for duellists, and the smell of arnica.

story_crest_academy/stage_glass_annex.alt: The Glass Annex: A glasshouse at the end of the cloister where Princess Isolde lives among orange trees her mother planted.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_w.alt: The North Gate Watch House: A one-room stone hut beside the north gate with a brazier, a bunk, a rack for a cudgel and a lantern, and a stool by the door where the night watchman is supposed to stay awake.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_l.alt: The Lockup: A stone cell under the bell tower with one barred window at cobble height, a bench, a bucket, and two circuit men on the door who are bored and not cruel.

story_crest_academy/stage_lowmarket.alt: Lowmarket: The town at the foot of the cliff stairs: a market square where the Open Trial was held, stalls, washing lines, and the Broken Spur, a tavern where commoners bet on the scholar and the Society drinks once a year.

story_crest_academy/seraphine.alt: Lady Seraphine Aldric, The rival. First of this year’s intake, heir of the empire’s sword-masters, and the woman who challenged you before you had unpacked

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_reeve.alt: The Reeve’s House: The tallest house in Kettlecross, three storeys of good stone facing the river, with a polished brass knocker and an office on the ground floor where the reeve keeps a strongbox.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_north_gate.alt: The North Gate: The city’s north wall and its one gate, where refugees from the fog come in and soldiers go out.

story_crest_academy/mio.alt: Mio Fenn, The maid-knight assigned to you: carries your bag, brings your supper, and knows the Ring Code better than the people who duel by it

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_f.alt: The Ferry Landing: A timber jetty on the brown river where Nell’s ferry sits chained by order of the circuit, the salt barge Honest Weight is moored with its plank down, and the reeds below hide things people want found.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_edge_of_sti.alt: The Edge of the Stilling: Four hours north, where the grey begins.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_reeve.alt: The Reeve’s Cellar: A long, cold cellar under the reeve’s house with twelve salt barrels stencilled for the Lowmere Salt Bank, each one far too heavy for salt.

story_the_hero_s_spare/stage_tallow_row.alt: Tallow Row: The river quarter: candle works, eel smokehouses, barges tied three deep, and narrow lanes where nobody writes anything down.

story_the_hero_s_spare/kai.alt: Kai Brandt, The hero the circle marked: a bike courier from your world, taken mid-delivery

story_the_hero_s_spare/mira.alt: Mira Holt, Sergeant of the Circle Wardens, and the sword that is supposed to send you back

story_crest_academy/cover.alt: Cover art for Crest Academy: Five points to spend. Ten seconds left.

story_crest_academy/isolde.alt: Princess Isolde of Vael, The Emperor’s third daughter, a second-year who lives among orange trees and needs the scholarship to survive the vote

story_pack_rank/stage_the_circle.alt: The Circle: The old courtyard, flagstones worn smooth, and in the middle a ring of chalk six paces across that Coach Stagg redraws every evening.

story_pack_rank/stage_long_hall.alt: The Long Hall: The dining hall: eleven long tables in rank order, the first one under the painted Order and the last one by the kitchen hatch.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_b.alt: The Honest Weight: The Lowmere Salt Bank’s barge: sixty feet of tarred deck, a hold half full of real salt, two bargemen who do not ask questions, and a stern cabin with a desk, a lamp and a factor in it.

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_h.alt: The Hill Road: A switchback track of red gravel up the dragon’s hill, steep enough to stop for breath every bend.

story_pack_rank/stage_guest_room.alt: The Gatehouse Room: No den would take a human, so the Faculty put you in the old gatekeeper’s room above the lower gate: one bed, one desk, a window onto the road down to town, and a door that does not lock properly.

story_pack_rank/stage_hill_den.alt: The Hill Pack House: A long, low stone house on the hill side of the grounds where the wolves and their friends sleep in one big bunk room.

story_crest_academy/brannoch.alt: Instructor Halden Brannoch, Master of the Ring. Calls every duel, keeps every clause, and wears a crest that reads far too low for a former imperial champion

story_crest_academy/piers.alt: Lord Piers Hallam, Second-year Society duellist with gambling debts, Varro’s errand-runner, and the first name on tomorrow’s Ladder against you

story_three_skills_a_morning/stage_the_h.alt: The Hollow: The scorched bowl at the top of the hill, wide enough to hold the whole of Ford Square twice over, floored with glassy black rock and two centuries of bones from the river’s cattle.

story_the_hero_s_spare/odile.alt: Odile Castine, High Priestess of the Church of the Circle. She lit the circle and turned the sandglass

story_the_hero_s_spare/ilsabet.alt: Ilsabet Corvane, Crown Princess and acting regent while her father is said to have a fever

story_crest_academy/varro.alt: Lord Ansel Varro, Third-year, captain of the Rail Society, top of the challenge board, and the pleasant man holding the pencil

story_three_skills_a_morning/nell.alt: Nell Farrow, Ferry hand, former pickpocket, and the woman they are hanging at noon

story_the_hero_s_spare/emeric.alt: Emeric Dahl, The cathedral Archivist, who recorded the last Returning as a junior clerk

story_the_hero_s_spare/severin.alt: Severin Ashby, Knight-Captain of the Circle Guard, the church’s sworn sword, who believes every spare is the fog in disguise

story_three_skills_a_morning/garrot.alt: Sir Garrot Dunmere, The lord’s circuit justiciar, who holds the dawn assize and hangs at noon

story_the_hero_s_spare/bet.alt: Bet Tallis, Eel smoker and seller of new names in Tallow Row

story_pack_rank/stage_boiler_room.alt: The Boiler Room: Under the Long Hall, warm, loud and lit orange by the boiler’s grate.

story_pack_rank/stage_north_stair.alt: The North Stair: A narrow stone stair from the Long Hall up to the archive and the third-years’ corridor, four minutes quicker than the south stair.

story_pack_rank/stage_sunward_house.alt: Sunward House: The lions’ house, south-facing and old money: deep carpets, a dining room with silver on the table, and portraits of every first rank Sunward has produced, and it has produced most of them.

story_pack_rank/stage_the_warren.alt: The Courier Loft: The Warren’s loft above the old stables: hammocks, pigeonholes stuffed with notes, a map of the grounds drawn on the wall in six colours of ink, and the cheapest beds in the school.

story_three_skills_a_morning/haldis.alt: Haldis, The dragon who owns the hill, the ford and the town’s lease, and the party who was robbed

story_the_hero_s_spare/cover.alt: Cover art for The Hero’s Spare: Summoned by mistake. Sent back by sword.

story_three_skills_a_morning/ysolde.alt: Ysolde Marr, Keeper of the Crooked Kettle, who gave the stranger a bed on credit

story_pack_rank/stage_the_archive.alt: The Order Archive: A long room under the roof where every year’s final Order is carved into a wooden board and hung, one board a year, back a hundred and twenty years.

story_three_skills_a_morning/cotter.alt: Anselm Cotter, The town reeve, who keeps the keys and the ledgers, and who found the coin in her boot

story_three_skills_a_morning/pim.alt: Pim Atwater, The night watchman whose testimony is hanging Nell

story_pack_rank/stage_the_gate.alt: The Lower Gate: The academy’s lower gate, iron and always open, with a bus shelter outside it on the town road.

story_pack_rank/stage_infirmary.alt: The Infirmary: Six iron beds, a nurse who has seen every kind of Circle injury there is, and a jar of sweets for anyone who yields politely.

story_pack_rank/stage_the_ridge.alt: The Ridge Course: Eleven kilometres of path along the bare ridge above the academy, marked by stone cairns and run at dawn by the wolves.

story_three_skills_a_morning/quell.alt: Corra Quell, Factor of the Lowmere Salt Bank, aboard the barge, collecting the reeve’s debt

story_pack_rank/stage_lantern_street.alt: Lantern Street: The one street of the market town below the academy: a noodle stall, a laundrette, a hardware shop, the bus stop and a tea house that serves students on condition they do not settle anything inside it.

story_pack_rank/ruka.alt: Ruka Varn, Second on the Order, leader of the Hill Pack, and the wolf whose tray is on your table

story_pack_rank/lio.alt: Lio Solenne, First on the Order for two years, heir to Sunward House, and the one person in the school nobody has ever touched

story_pack_rank/pim.alt: Pim Hollowell, Last on the Order, courier for the Warren, and the cheapest rank on the wall to take

story_pack_rank/stagg.alt: Halvard Stagg, Combat coach and referee of the Circle. Everybody calls him Coach Stagg

story_pack_rank/fenn.alt: Fenn Asari, Bookmaker. Runs the odds on every bout in the school from the boiler room

story_pack_rank/bryn.alt: Bryn Holt, Fourth on the Order, Lio’s den second, and the one who keeps the door at Sunward House

story_pack_rank/cover.alt: Cover art for Pack Rank: The only human. The wolf wants you first.

story_three_skills_a_morning/cover.alt: Cover art for Three Skills a Morning: Three skills. Keep one. She hangs at noon.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_roof.alt: The Roof Garden: Planters, two benches, the whole river and the city lights behind it.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_room.alt: Bedroom, 12C: The room you both have an email for.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_living_.alt: 12C, Living Room: A sofa that folds out into a bed nobody would choose, a kitchenette with two hobs and a kettle, a bathroom with a latch and one shelf to fight over, and a Residence Life welcome pack on the counter.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_floor_twelv.alt: The Twelfth Floor: Eleven doors, a lounge with a broken air hockey table, a laundry room that eats coins, Kit’s room at the far end, and the lifts.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_lobby.alt: Linden House Lobby: Glass doors, key-card gates, a staffed front desk, a wall of mailboxes and a noticeboard.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_quad.alt: The Quad: Four paths, one fountain, a campus café with a queue out of the door, and three thousand people who have all seen her face.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_housing_off.alt: The Housing Office: A ticket machine, a waiting room with forty chairs and sixty people, and Ms.

story_roommate_lottery/stage_hargrove_ha.alt: Hargrove Hall: The oldest dorm on campus: radiators that knock, a shared bathroom down the corridor, and Ben’s room on the third floor with exactly enough floor for one sleeping bag and a roommate who snores like a leaf blower.

story_roommate_lottery/haneul.alt: Haneul Seo, Yuri’s manager, who arrives with a ring light and a contract

story_roommate_lottery/stage_the_old_bui.alt: Her Old Building: A smart building downtown with a doorman and a lobby full of plants.

story_human_row_three/stage_the_cloister.alt: The Cloister: The square at the heart of Hollowmere: a covered arcade round a yard with a well and a bell tower, a notice board three layers deep, and doorways to everything.

story_roommate_lottery/yuri.alt: Yuri Sakamoto, Your roommate until Friday, and the most famous person on campus

story_human_row_three/stage_homeroom.alt: Homeroom: A tiered classroom under the bell tower: five rows of desks scored by claws and scorched in one corner, thirty students of thirty kinds, and a lectern at the front with the register chained to it.

story_human_row_three/stage_great_hall.alt: The Great Hall: Five long House tables under a ceiling of living roots, a head table where Mr.

story_human_row_three/stage_guest_room.alt: The Guest Room: The room kept for the human exchange student, at the top of the old tower stair, opened this week for the first time in forty-one years.

story_roommate_lottery/ben.alt: Ben Castillo, Your best friend since first-year orientation, a film student with a floor you can sleep on

story_human_row_three/key.alt: Key art for Human, Row Three

story_roommate_lottery/kit.alt: Kit Navarro, The resident assistant for the twelfth floor, who has to write this up

story_roommate_lottery/cover.alt: Cover art for Roommate Lottery: Your roommate has two million followers.

story_roommate_lottery/jonah.alt: Jonah Whitlock, Your neighbour in 12D, who is always filming something

story_human_row_three/stage_the_roost.alt: The Roost: The top of the bell tower, open to the wind on three sides: pigeonholes for the academy post, hammocks slung between the bell beams, and a slate board where Sylph chalks the odds on everything.

story_human_row_three/stage_council_cham.alt: The Council Chamber: Cellar House’s rooms, one floor below ground and lit only by candles: a long table that seats five Houses, two teapots that are not for the same thing, and the five iron lanterns waiting on a sideboard.

story_human_row_three/stage_the_stacks.alt: The Stacks: The academy library goes down instead of up: nine levels of shelves cut into the rock under the cliff, joined by a stair that spirals round a shaft of lamplight.

story_human_row_three/stage_deep_stacks.alt: The Bottom of the Stacks: Below the ninth level, where the stair stops pretending to be part of a library: a room of lamps, a kettle on a spirit stove, a camp bed, a hand-knitted rug and forty-one years of books nobody has borrowed.

story_roommate_lottery/park.alt: Park Eun-ha, The housing coordinator who has to decide who keeps 12C

story_human_row_three/stage_gate_yard.alt: The Gate Yard: The wardens’ yard inside the academy gate, packed earth and iron.

story_human_row_three/stage_lake_dock.alt: The Mere: At the bottom of the cliff stair: a black lake so still it holds the academy upside down, a Deep House boathouse on stilts, and a long dock that runs out further than it needs to.

story_human_row_three/stage_the_briar.alt: The Briar Gate: The end of the warden road: a wall of black thorn and green leaf a mile deep and higher than the bell tower, running out of sight both ways, with one arched gate through it and a brass bell to ring the Exchange Office on the far side.

story_human_row_three/stage_lanternside.alt: Lanternside: The town at the foot of the academy hill, outside the wall and outside the ward: a crooked market street of lamp-makers, a tea house that serves three kinds of tea and one kind of something else, a tailor who measures everybody for a tail-hole, and a great many people who have never seen a human and would like a closer look.

story_human_row_three/vey.alt: Countess Ottilie Vey, Head of the student Council and of Cellar House, a vampire who has refused to graduate for forty-four years

story_human_row_three/garra.alt: Ishiko, Oni of Gate House, heir to the wardens, and the student sitting directly behind you

story_human_row_three/sylph.alt: Sylph, Harpy of the Roost, academy post-runner, and the bookmaker taking bets on how long you last

story_human_row_three/teague.alt: Teague, Kelpie, head of Deep House, who keeps the boathouse on the Mere and makes every conversation a bargain

story_human_row_three/bones.alt: Mr. Bones, Homeroom teacher, keeper of the register and head of Bone House, a skeleton who has taken roll twice a day for eighty-three years

story_human_row_three/keeper.alt: The Keeper, Keeper of the bottom of the Stacks, whom most of the school believes is a ghost

story_human_row_three/cover.alt: Cover art for Human, Row Three: Thirty monsters. Every head turns to you.

story_one_year_bride/stage_teos.alt: Teo’s: Twelve tables, a charcoal grill behind a counter of salt-bleached wood, and a neon sign whose apostrophe flickers.

story_one_year_bride/stage_the_pier.alt: The Old Pier: Two hundred metres of timber over grey-green water: fishing lines, lamp posts with a gull on every one, and the new planks from the storm repairs paler than the old.

story_one_year_bride/stage_the_flat.alt: The Flat Above Teo’s: One bedroom, one sofa eight inches too short for anybody, a kitchenette with a two-ring hob, a balcony the size of a doormat over the water, and a bathroom door that has not locked since before you were born.

story_one_year_bride/stage_the_boathouse.alt: Teo’s Boathouse: A converted boathouse under the land end of the pier, where Teo has lived alone since your grandmother died.

story_thin_walls/stage_flat_3c.alt: Flat 3C: The mirror image of yours, with half the furniture.

story_thin_walls/stage_the_wall.alt: The Wall: Your bedroom in Flat 3B, and in particular the desk pushed against its east wall.

story_thin_walls/stage_flat_3b.alt: Flat 3B: Two bedrooms and a kitchen-living room with a sofa that came with the lease.

story_thin_walls/stage_the_landing.alt: The Third-Floor Landing: Two front doors eleven steps apart, 3B and 3C, on bare boards that announce everybody.

story_one_year_bride/stage_the_station.alt: Sorrel Bay Station: Two platforms and a ticket machine that only takes coins.

story_one_year_bride/stage_the_beach.alt: The Shingle Beach: A strip of grey stones under the legs of the pier, where the town launches its paper lanterns in autumn and where you go to say something nobody on the pier should hear.

story_one_year_bride/stage_harbour_stree.alt: Harbour Street: The town’s one real street: the fish market, a bakery with a back table, the bank where the debt lives, the registry office where you got married this afternoon, and the station steps at the top of the hill.

story_one_year_bride/stage_gull_point.alt: The Cliff House: Chiyo Kurosawa’s house on the headland across the bay: shutters closed since winter, a walled garden of lemon trees gone wild, and a brass telescope in the upstairs window, pointed at the end of your grandfather’s pier.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Long Kitchen: The palace kitchens: a vaulted room a hundred feet long, six hearths, a larder the size of a chapel and cooks who do not want a stranger near their fire.

The Heroes’ Wing: Guest apartments for three: three bedrooms with three beds, a common room with one couch, a balcony over the palace roofs, and a bell-pull that summons a servant who is clearly afraid of Rin.
The Drill Yard: A sanded yard ringed by the guardhouse and the stables, where Sir Bastian’s forty knights drill at dawn.

story_one_year_bride/stage_seaview_hotel.alt: The Kurosawa Seaview: Glass and white stone on the far side of the harbour, the only hotel in town, owned by Reina’s father.

story_thin_walls/stage_the_roof.alt: The Roof: A flat tar roof with a knee-high parapet, two deckchairs nobody owns, and Sam’s microphone stand weighted with a brick.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Hall of Calling: A vaulted stone hall under the High Chapel, cold even in summer.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/key.alt: Key art for Three Heroines and a Porter

story_thin_walls/stage_lamplight_cafe.alt: The Lamplight: A 24-hour café with nine tables, a counter Theo leans on, a pastry case that is mostly crumbs after midnight, and a corner table by the window that looks straight up at the third floor of 14 Larkin Street.

story_thin_walls/stage_the_canal.alt: The Canal Path: A towpath behind Larkin Street that runs a mile along black water to the back gate of the faculty.

story_thin_walls/stage_larkin_street.alt: Larkin Street: A narrow street of converted terraces with bins out on the wrong day.

story_thin_walls/stage_faculty_hall.alt: The Faculty of Law: An old stone building with a draughty main hall, the final-year rank list pinned under glass by the stairs, and doors off to the library, the Old Court and the staff corridor.

story_one_year_bride/reina.alt: Reina Kurosawa, Your wife of six hours. A lawyer from the city with a deadline, a contract and twelve rules

story_one_year_bride/teo.alt: Teodoro Reyes, Your grandfather. He opened the grill at the end of the pier fifty-one years ago and still runs it, loudly

story_one_year_bride/bo.alt: Bo-mi Choi, Front of house at Teo’s for thirty-one years, owner of the kiosk at the pier gate, and the town’s news service

story_seven_years_early/stage_blue_hour.alt: Blue Hour Café: A narrow café on Canal Street with fogged windows, mismatched chairs and a counter where the startup crowd orders oat flat whites and talks too loudly about money.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Cloister: The Choir’s quarters: a square walk of pillars round an herb garden, cells for the priests, the vestry door into the Hall of Calling, a locked iron door to the archive, and a green door in the wall to a garden nobody is meant to visit.

story_one_year_bride/felix.alt: Felix Arden, The estate’s lawyer and Reina’s ex-fiancé, who decides at the anniversary whether the marriage was real

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Glass Tower: The Choir’s mage tower: nine floors of lenses, burn-marked tables and books that hum when you open them.

story_one_year_bride/cover.alt: Cover art for One-Year Bride: Your wife of six hours has twelve rules.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Mercy Ward: A long ward in the palace’s lower court: forty beds of soldiers brought back from the east.

story_seven_years_early/stage_your_flat.alt: Your Flat: One room and a kitchenette above a launderette, warm from the dryers downstairs.

story_thin_walls/stage_law_library.alt: The Law Library: Open all night in finals: four floors of law reports, carrels with names pencilled on them, and a window table where you can see everybody who comes in.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Sealed Archive: A long low room of shelves and chained books under the cloister.
The Still Garden: A walled garden behind the cloister, very quiet.

story_seven_years_early/key.alt: Key art for Seven Years Early

story_seven_years_early/stage_canal_stre.alt: Canal Street: The old warehouse district along the canal, where the city’s startups rent floors in former mills: a tram stop, three cafés, the Lucky Bowl noodle shop with its steamed-up window, and a lot of people in good trainers pitching each other on the pavement.

story_seven_years_early/stage_osei_offic.alt: Osei’s Office: Two rooms above the Lucky Bowl noodle shop: filing cabinets to the ceiling, a brass desk timer, a fern that has outlived two partners, and Wendell Osei, who bills by the quarter hour and has never once filed anything late.

story_one_year_bride/masaru.alt: Masaru Kurosawa, Reina’s father, chairman of Kurosawa Seaview Resorts, with a buyer waiting for her grandmother’s house

story_thin_walls/stage_the_old_court.alt: The Old Court: A real courtroom, moved stone by stone into the faculty a century ago.

story_thin_walls/stage_lund_office.alt: Lund’s Office: A narrow room at the end of the staff corridor.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_f.alt: Founders’ Quad: A square of lawn the size of a football pitch, cut by four paths, with the student union on one side, the library on another, and four hundred people eating lunch on the benches in between.

story_thin_walls/nadia.alt: Nadia Cho, First place in your year three years running, and since Sunday the voice on the other side of your bedroom wall

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_u.alt: The Union Roof: A flat roof behind the fire door whose alarm has not worked since spring.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_c.alt: The Council Office: The top floor of the union: a long room with eleven desks, a whiteboard of budget lines, and one tidy desk by the window with a nameplate nobody else touches.

story_thin_walls/sam.alt: Sam Ferreira, Your flatmate in 3B, a final-year sound student who records everything and has already named the wall

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_s.alt: The Student Union: Five floors of noise: a food court on the ground floor, club rooms above it, the council office on the top floor, and a basement where the campus paper is made.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/key.alt: Key art for Ice Queen’s Fake Boyfriend

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Side Gate: The servants’ and deliveries’ gate in the palace’s west wall: a lantern, a bar, a bench for the guard, and carts of turnips and firewood coming in all day.

story_thin_walls/cover.alt: Cover art for Thin Walls: Your rival can hear you through the wall.

story_seven_years_early/stage_founders_h.alt: Founders’ Hall: A converted tram depot that is now the city’s startup accelerator: long tables, a coffee machine nobody can work, and a stage at one end with a big screen.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Porters’ Hall: A long timber hall at the bottom of the market street: benches, a soup cauldron, tally sticks on hooks and two hundred people the crystal read as nothing.

story_thin_walls/theo.alt: Theo Cho, Her older brother. Runs the night shift at the café across the road, and left the same law faculty six years ago

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/stage_.alt: The Low Market: The city below the palace walls: awnings, carts, a fish smell, spice stalls selling red pods that are nearly chilli, and a whole street where nobody moves a load without a porter’s strap.
The East Road: The road out of the east gate toward the river Wend, a day’s march away.

story_seven_years_early/stage_vos_tower.alt: Vos Calder Tower: Forty floors of glass at the end of Canal Street, with Vos Calder Ventures at the top: a reception desk of white stone, a view of the whole river, and a waiting room where founders sit for an hour to get ninety seconds.

story_seven_years_early/stage_lowtide.alt: Lowtide Boathouse: A converted boathouse on the river where Naomi Ito’s whole fund fits in one room: one desk, one whiteboard covered in other people’s numbers, a kettle, and a wooden rowing boat she has been repairing for two years.

story_seven_years_early/stage_victor_lof.alt: Victor’s Loft: The top floor of an old mill, all brick and glass, with a long kitchen nobody cooks in and a wall of empty frames waiting for magazine covers he has not been on yet.

story_seven_years_early/stage_cold_case_.alt: The Cold Case Annex: The basement of Westharbor Police headquarters: a corridor of banker’s boxes, one window at pavement level and three desks, two of them empty.

story_thin_walls/elliot.alt: Elliot Ashby, Third in the year by three tenths of a mark, and the only person who wins if either finalist is disqualified

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_c.alt: The Courier Newsroom: A basement room under the union with no windows, six old computers, a sofa somebody clearly sleeps on, and a wall of front pages going back forty years.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_l.alt: Linden House, Room 318: Your room on the third floor of a loud residence: a bed, a desk, a window that does not shut properly, a kettle you are not allowed to have, and a door your sister has a key to for emergencies, which she defines broadly.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_s.alt: Old Hall, Room Twelve: A narrow seminar room in the oldest building on campus: one long table, fourteen chairs, a radiator that knocks, and Professor Ito’s office through the door at the back, full of books stacked sideways and an armchair with a coat over it.

story_thin_walls/lund.alt: Professor Ingrid Lund, Chair of Advocacy. She wrote the moot problem, chairs the bench, and decides who gets the clerkship

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_t.alt: The Boathouse: A long wooden boathouse on the lake at the bottom of campus: the rowing club below, a terrace restaurant above where the business school eats on somebody else’s card.
The Library Reading Room: A vaulted reading room open all night since three weeks ago, when the council president reversed her own rule.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/rin.alt: Rin Morikawa, Your club captain, read tonight as a Sword Saint. She wants you off the road east

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/cover.alt: Cover art for Three Heroines and a Porter: They got SSS classes. You got nothing.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/maya.alt: Maya Tanabe, Physics postgraduate, read tonight as an Archmage. She wants you close

story_seven_years_early/stage_seventh_fl.alt: The Seventh Floor: The seventh floor of the Halcott Building, empty and to let: bare concrete, dust sheets, rain on tall windows.

story_seven_years_early/stage_st_brigids.alt: St. Brigid’s Hospital: The cardiology walk-in on the ground floor of St.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_h.alt: The Hollis Townhouse: A tall cream house on a quiet square in the old town: a dining table for fourteen set for three, a study with its door shut but not locked, and a portrait of Akane’s late father in the hall that she walks past without looking.

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/bastia.alt: Sir Bastian Vell, Knight-commander of the heroes’ escort, with written orders to put you out

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/saki.alt: Saki Hirose, Was training as a nurse, read tonight as a Saint. She wants you to decide for yourself

story_seven_years_early/stage_art_colleg.alt: Westharbor College of Art: A big old building full of studios that smell of turpentine and toast.

story_seven_years_early/victor.alt: Victor Lane, The co-founder who stole your company and let you die, on the morning you first met him

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_m.alt: Mercer Street: The strip outside the main gate: a ramen counter open until two, a stationer’s with a flat above it, the bus stop for the old town, and a bakery that opens at six and is run by a woman who knows Darren Cole’s order by heart.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/stage_g.alt: The Great Hall: The university’s oldest and grandest room, a hammer-beam roof and tall windows, used three times a year.

story_seven_years_early/naomi.alt: Naomi Ito, Seed investor at Lowtide Capital, and the meeting you skipped last time

story_seven_years_early/cover.alt: Cover art for Seven Years Early: Same handshake. You know how it ends.

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/cover.alt: Cover art for Ice Queen’s Fake Boyfriend: Six days to fake it. She chose you. Why?

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/odessa.alt: Odessa Marrin, High Cantor of the Choir, who performed the Calling

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/darren.alt: Darren Cole, Heir to the Cole Group, business-school graduate student, the name printed next to hers

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/hesper.alt: Hesper, The archer of the last Calling, forty-one years on, living in the Choir’s walled garden

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/akane.alt: Akane Hollis, Student council president, third year, the one the whole campus calls the Ice Queen

story_three_heroines_and_a_porter/grete.alt: Grete Holm, Forewoman of the Porters’ Hall, the guild of everybody the crystal read as nothing

story_seven_years_early/ruiz.alt: Detective Celia Ruiz, Cold-case detective who never believed Victor’s first partner died by accident

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/mei.alt: Mei, Your older sister, final-year journalism student, and editor of the campus paper

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/evelyn.alt: Evelyn Hollis, Akane’s mother, chief executive of the family firm Hollis & Lane

story_seven_years_early/vos.alt: Arden Vos, Managing partner of Vos Calder Ventures, the biggest money in the city

story_ice_queen_s_fake_boyfriend/ito.alt: Professor Daisuke Ito, Rhetoric professor and faculty adviser to the student council

story_seven_years_early/sol.alt: Sol, Your younger sister, in her final year at art college, asleep on your sofa

story_seven_years_early/osei.alt: Wendell Osei, Patent attorney above the noodle shop, and the fastest on Canal Street

story_one_week_she_said/stage_tamura_fla.alt: Mrs. Tamura’s Rooms, 1A: The landlady’s ground-floor rooms: a hallway of polished shoes, a kitchen that smells of broth, a spare room kept made up for a son who never visits, a framed copy of the house rules by the door, and a shoe cupboard she does not like people opening.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_apartment_.alt: Apartment 2C: Your one-bedroom on the second floor: an entryway barely wide enough for two pairs of shoes, a kitchen strip with a two-ring hob, a main room with a low table and a sofa that folds out into a bad bed, a bedroom door that sticks, one bathroom, and a balcony just wide enough for the washing machine.

story_one_week_she_said/key.alt: Key art for One Week, She Said

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_walkwa.alt: The Outside Walkway: The open-air corridor along the second floor of Hinode Court, with a concrete stair at each end and a railing that drips when it rains.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_arcade.alt: Kitamachi Arcade: A covered shopping street running from your road to the station: a convenience store that never closes, a laundromat with one good dryer, a ramen counter with Jun’s apartment above it, a business hotel with its front desk just inside the automatic doors, and the bus stop at the near end where the last bus leaves at twenty to midnight.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_riverb.alt: The River Embankment: A long concrete embankment with a running path, a row of bare cherry trees, a set of steps down to the water, and a bench under the railway bridge where nobody can hear you over the trains.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_office.alt: Tsubame Logistics, Fourth Floor: The open-plan floor of a freight company that moves other people’s furniture across the country: forty desks, a whiteboard of delivery routes, a manager in a glass box, a kitchenette fridge that is a crime scene, and your desk by the window with Jun’s mess spilling onto it.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_unit_1406.alt: Apartment 1406: Kenta’s fourteenth-floor apartment: white walls, a harbour view, nothing out of place, and every trace of Mika boxed and taped in the spare room with her name on the boxes in his neat handwriting.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_kenta_towe.alt: Harbourline Tower: A new glass apartment tower on the waterfront, with a show-suite on the ground floor where Kenta sells the units upstairs, a lobby with a concierge desk and a night concierge who likes him, and lifts that need a key card past the third floor.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_aya_salon.alt: Aya’s Salon: Two chairs, one basin, a radio tuned to a station nobody else likes, a wall of photographs of haircuts Aya is proud of, and a back room with a kettle and a sofa where she does her accounts and her worrying.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/stage_t.alt: The Vestry: A narrow room behind the altar with a table, the register in a leather cover, the officiant’s folder, a box of tissues nobody has opened, and a window onto nothing but sea.
The Terrace Bar: A stone terrace over the sea with a long brass bar, twenty tables, and a view that makes people say things they did not plan to.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/key.alt: Key art for Back Row at My Own Wedding

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/stage_t.alt: The Wisteria Lawn: A long lawn between the chapel and the hotel under a hundred-year-old wisteria arch, where the photographs happen and where every guest who wants a cigarette or a cry ends up.

The Glass Chapel: A chapel of white-painted iron and glass on the very edge of the cliff: rows of white chairs with every one taken, wisteria trained over the roof, and the sea filling every window behind the altar.

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_new_st.alt: The New Studio: A ground-floor studio across the city in a building with a cats-welcome sign on the door: one room, a kitchenette, a sliding door onto a strip of garden, and a letting agent who will hand over a key on a paper tag next Sunday at ten if the paperwork is complete by five on Friday.

story_one_week_she_said/mika.alt: Mika Arai, The classmate who made your final year of school a misery, now soaked on your doorstep asking for eight nights

story_one_week_she_said/jun.alt: Jun Kuroda, Your coworker at the next desk, and the only person you ever told about school

story_one_week_she_said/aya.alt: Aya, Your older sister. Owns a two-chair salon across the river, and knows more about tonight than she has said

story_one_week_she_said/stage_the_izakay.alt: The Red Lantern: A yakitori bar two streets past the station with a long upstairs room Daisuke has booked for the eight-year class reunion: thirty cushions, a projector pointed at a sliding door, and a counter downstairs where Daisuke holds court every night this week.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/stage_t.alt: The Long Room: The ballroom: a long gilded room with twelve windows onto the sea, a head table, a dance floor, a four-tier cake with two names iced on it, and a microphone on a stand that has been switched on since five.

The Lobby: The Hale’s old front hall: black and white tiles, a front desk with a brass bell, a staircase that splits in two, four generations of Hales in oil on the walls, and a porter who has known you for thirty years and is pretending very hard not to look at you.
The Bridal Suite: The top-floor suite with the round turret window, an empty dress bag, three phone chargers, a breakfast tray nobody touched, and a desk covered in papers that are not about flowers.

The Events Office: A windowless basement office with three monitors, a wall of run sheets, a camp bed folded behind the door, a printer still warm, and a box marked SPOILS full of cards that were wrong this morning.
The Kitchens: Steel counters, forty staff, a pass that never stops, and at the far end the flower cold room with its heavy door and round window.

story_one_week_she_said/kenta.alt: Kenta Yasuda, Mika’s ex-fiancé. Sales manager at a waterfront tower, everybody’s favourite dinner guest, and the name on everything she owned

story_one_week_she_said/tamura.alt: Fumiko Tamura, Your landlady. Lives in 1A, sweeps the walkway at half past five, and enforces the no-pets clause with her whole heart

story_one_week_she_said/daisuke.alt: Daisuke Ueno, Your old classmate. Organising the eight-year reunion, and still calling you what Mika named you

story_one_week_she_said/cover.alt: Cover art for One Week, She Said: Your old tormentor. Your sofa. One week.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/stage_c.alt: Grandmother’s Study: A wood-panelled room in the old wing with the curtains always open, a desk the size of a rowing boat, a silver-framed photograph from 1966, and a cream envelope set exactly in the middle of the blotter.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/stage_t.alt: The Car Park: Gravel, rows of guests’ cars, a white car with ribbons on it that nobody has told what to do, and yours, still ticking from the coast road, with the driver’s door not quite shut.
The Cliff Path: A narrow path along the cliff top with a rail on the sea side, gorse on the other, and a bench with a brass plate for Edwin Hale.
The Old Boathouse: A tarred wooden boathouse at the foot of the cliff steps, full of oars and a rowing boat nobody has taken out since your grandfather died.

The Gatehouse: The stone cottage at the bottom of the drive where the groom’s party stayed: three bedrooms, a sofa with a dent in it, last night’s bottles, your bag, and your brother’s own jacket over the back of a chair, where he left it when he put on yours.
