story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/cover.alt: Cover art for Back Row at My Own Wedding: Your bride is marrying your brother.

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/elena.alt: Elena Ward, The bride. Your fiancée until some time this morning, a litigation lawyer, and the only person in the chapel with a deadline

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/sami.alt: Sami Rahal, Your best friend since university, your best man, and a paramedic who is treating this as an emergency

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/marcus.alt: Marcus Hale, Your older brother, standing at the altar in your suit

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/june.alt: June Arden, Events manager at the Hale, who planned this wedding with you for eleven months

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/constan.alt: Constance Hale, Your grandmother. Owner of the Hale for fifty-eight years, and the only person in the chapel who is not surprised

story_back_row_at_my_own_wedding/benny.alt: Benny Castellano, The wedding photographer, hired by June, who has shot six hundred weddings and photographs everything

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_d.alt: The Drowned Lantern: A low dice house under the quay, lit by lanterns sunk in water barrels.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_w.alt: The Rivergate Cells: Six stone cells under the river gate: wet straw, a slit window at the height of the water, and a turnkey’s desk with a pot of porridge on the brazier.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/key.alt: Key art for The Morning of the Gallows

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_g.alt: The Rivergate Yard: The garrison yard above the cells: a drill square, the company barracks, a gate down to the river market and a road up into the city.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_r.alt: The River Market: A long cobbled quay of bread stalls, fish tubs and boats tied three deep.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_s.alt: The South Road: Beyond the last mooring the river widens and the road follows it south toward the border hills.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_t.alt: Tollmarket Green: The city’s central square: market crosses, the toll house, and a patch of trampled grass with a gallows on it.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_h.alt: The Hangman’s House: A narrow house on the edge of the green with its shutters always open.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_v.alt: The Vane House: A tall, quiet townhouse full of law books, with a walled garden and a fig tree.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_h.alt: The Hall of Pleas: The Crown’s court: a cold stone hall with a public gallery, a dock, and the long table where the Crown’s Advocate stands.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_t.alt: The Crownhold: The old King’s palace on the hill: a great hall hung with the banners of every reign, a high table on a dais, the King’s private cellar under it, and a sickroom where an old man’s hands will not stop shaking.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/stage_a.alt: Ashcourt: The Prince’s house beside the palace gardens: a long room full of petitioners, a counting room where his secretary keeps the books, and a glasshouse he tends himself, warm and green all year.
The Stillroom: A windowless brick room behind the glasshouse: drying racks of small blue flowers, a copper still, stoppered vials in rows, and a cushioned stool where the Prince sits to work.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/key.alt: Key art for The Maid Owns the House Now

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Front Hall: A marble hall two storeys high, with a grand staircase curving up to the bedroom floor.
The Servants’ Stair: A narrow stone-and-oak stair behind the baize door, climbing from the kitchen to the attic in four steep flights with a landing at every floor.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/isra.alt: Lady Isra Vane, The Crown’s Advocate and your betrothed. She signed your death warrant, and this morning she broke you out

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/corvin.alt: Prince Corvin, The King’s only son and heir. Reformer, gardener, and the man who comes down to your cell at nine

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Attic Rooms: The old servants’ bedrooms under the slates: six narrow rooms off a sloping corridor, iron bedsteads, a water tank that knocks at night, and a box room at the end with its door wedged shut from inside.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/hob.alt: Sergeant Hob Garrow, Your old sergeant, now turnkey of the Rivergate cells. Asleep at his desk when the story starts

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Kitchen: Below stairs and the warmest room in the house: a black iron range, a scrubbed table long enough for twelve, copper pans the bailiffs left because they were too heavy, and a board of brass bells labelled with rooms that have nobody in them.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/tull.alt: Hangman Tull, Hangman of Vellmark for forty-one years, and one of three people who remember the morning you died

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/sabine.alt: Sabine Orrel, Prince Corvin’s private secretary. Keeps his ledgers, his diary and his debts

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: Clara’s Office: The old housekeeper’s room, which Clara kept for herself instead of taking any of the forty upstairs.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_ro.alt: The Rope Field: A long cavern where every cut and snapped rope in the Deepway ends up, hanging from cracks in the ceiling like roots, hundreds of them, guild colours faded grey.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Ballroom: Sixty feet of sprung floor under a glass chandelier that has not been lit in six years, with tall windows onto the terrace and the sea.
The Cellar: Empty wine racks to the ceiling, because the receivers sold every bottle, and a cold that never leaves.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_su.alt: The Sump: The floor under the last floor, on no map.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Long Gallery: The bedroom floor: a corridor of family portraits, the ones the receivers judged worthless, and eleven bedrooms being made up for wedding guests.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_sp.alt: The Spine: A drain shaft as wide as a cart, climbing nine hundred feet from the Sump to the underside of the ninety-ninth floor, slick and ribbed with old water lines.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/key.alt: Key art for Cut Loose at Floor 99

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Rose Garden: Terraces of overgrown roses stepping down to a sea wall, a boathouse with a rotten jetty, a kitchen garden gone to seed, and a lawn where the wedding marquee will go if anybody can mow it.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_ec.alt: The Echo Shaft: A dry chimney in the Sump’s roof that carries sound down from every floor above.

story_the_morning_of_the_gallows/cover.alt: Cover art for The Morning of the Gallows: They hanged you once. Not this time.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: The Front Gates: Iron gates at the bottom of a lime-tree drive, with the family crest still worked into the top and a bell on a chain.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_agathe.alt: The Hollow: A dry, warm pocket behind the Rope Field where the lichen grows thickest.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: Pemberton Hall: A white stucco house on the opposite hill, newer and larger than Wrenhurst and less loved, with a glasshouse full of orchids and a study window that looks straight across the valley at your old bedroom.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_rust_c.alt: Rust Company Camp: Eleven tents, a cookfire and a salvage pile on a wide ledge on the ninety-eighth floor, one floor above the pit.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/midge.alt: Imogen Marsh, The under-maid Clara hired the afternoon of the auction, who has read about you in the society pages for years

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_ash_hall.alt: The Ash Hall: A hall the size of a train station, columns going up into the dark, where the raid fought the main horde three hours ago.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_glass_ga.alt: The Glass Gallery: A long corridor lined with panes of black glass taller than a person, most of them smashed by the raid.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_la.alt: The Last Door: The bottom of the charted Deepway.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/stage_.alt: Kestrel Bay: The harbour town under the cliff: a high street, a fish market, a bank with your family’s name still on a brass plaque by the door, a pub called the Anchor, the Gazette office, an antiques shop on the quay that asks no questions, and three hundred people who watched your family’s cars go past for a century and are enjoying this enormously.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_lo.alt: The Long Stair: Eight floors of switchback stair cut into the wall of a shaft, from Ninety-Eight up to Ninety.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_bell_sta.alt: The Bell Stair: A shaft going down further than any light reaches, a stone stair spiralling round its wall, and hundreds of dead bronze bells hanging on chains down the middle.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_the_mout.alt: The Mouth: The landing at the top of the ramp, just inside the gate.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/clara.alt: Clara Voss, The new owner of Wrenhurst House, and for eleven years before that, its maid

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_waycam.alt: Waycamp Ninety: The deepest guild camp in the Deepway: a stone platform on the ninetieth floor with a lift-cage on chains that runs up to the Rim, bunks, a Tally House clerk’s hut, and a board where crews chalk their names.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/key.alt: Key art for Cleanup Crew, E-Rank

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/pember.alt: Lady Honoria Pemberton, Owner of Pemberton Hall on the next hill and of the private bank that called in your house, who lost the auction by one bid

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/august.alt: Augustin, Your father, former master of Wrenhurst House, who vanished the night the bailiffs came

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_caretake.alt: The Caretaker’s Room: A small, tidy room off the stair that no raid map shows.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_tally_.alt: The Tally House: A stone hall at the lift-head where every delver who goes down is written in and every one who comes up is written out.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/hugo.alt: Hugo Ashworth, Butler of Wrenhurst House for forty-one years, who stayed on when the money went

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/silas.alt: Silas Dunmore, Agent for your father’s creditors, who keeps ringing at the gate

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_gilt_r.alt: The Gilt Rope Hall: The biggest guild hall in Lowmarch: marble, gold rope moulding on every doorframe, a long table for sixty, and a courtyard well that goes down further than any well should.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_gate_per.alt: The Cordon: Level B4 of a car park under a shopping centre that closed before it opened.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/stage_the_ri.alt: The Rim: The city of Lowmarch, built in rings around the mouth of the Deepway.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/lucan.alt: Lucan Harrow, Highwater’s leader and swordsman, your best friend since you shared a bunk at the delvers’ hostel at eighteen, and the man who cut your rope

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/voice.alt: The Voice, Something on the floor below the last floor, which speaks in a woman’s voice, knows your name, and has waited a very long time for somebody like you to fall

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_crew_yar.alt: Pyo Aftermath Depot: A garage in an industrial lane: two vans, a hose-down bay, a wall of lockers with numbers in marker, a sofa people sleep on between shifts, a kettle that never goes cold, and a shelf of cracked helmets nobody throws away.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_bureau_o.alt: The District Office: The Gate Bureau’s Garam district office: three floors of fluorescent light, a waiting room with numbered tickets, and in the basement the rank scanner, a white arch that reads what a person can do and prints it as a letter.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_night_po.alt: The Night Pot: A twenty-four-hour soup restaurant two streets from the depot, with a steamed-up window, eight stools and a pot of beef bone broth that has been going since before the gates.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_training.alt: The Basement Gate: Under the tower, behind two security doors, a small permanent gate the guild keeps open for training and for filming.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/stage_goldcres.alt: Goldcrest Tower: Forty floors of glass with the guild crest on top.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/taro.alt: Taro Kade, Captain of the Rust Company, a salvage crew that has come second to Highwater on every floor for three years, camped one floor above the pit

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/kes.alt: Kestrel Ivo, Highwater’s scout and archer, who agreed to the four shares because she did the arithmetic

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/elsbeth.alt: Elsbeth Marr, Highwater’s healer, who saw Lucan’s knife and looked at the wall

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/sallow.alt: Odran Sallow, Guildmaster of the Gilt Rope, eighty-eight, who founded the biggest guild in Lowmarch on a prize from Floor 61

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/hae_won.alt: Seo Hae-won, Goldcrest Guild’s S-rank healer, who stayed behind to fix a cleaner’s hand and is now pinned under a pillar

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/jin.alt: Kwak Jin-seok, Your crew partner for two years, E-rank like you, who talks in overtime rates and is carrying something he should not be

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/bran.alt: Bran Tull, Highwater’s shieldbearer, who was two flights up the stair carrying the lamp and was told you slipped

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/pyo.alt: Pyo Geum-ja, Owner of Pyo Aftermath Services and your boss, who calls everybody by their locker number and has never lost a crew member

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_champions_.alt: The Champions’ Cells: Stone rooms under the stands where the sixteen champions wait, strap their hands, and bleed quietly between bouts.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/baek.alt: Baek Mi-ran, District director of the Gate Bureau, who signed tonight’s clearance and decides at six whether to collapse the gate

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/hesper.alt: Hesper Moss, Tallykeeper of the Tally House, who wrote your name into the Book of the Lost on Lucan’s word

story_one_miracle_a_day/key.alt: Key art for One Miracle a Day

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_arbiter_ch.alt: The Unsworn Chapel: A bare chapel built into the arena wall, with no altar and no god.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_festival_s.alt: The Festival Streets: Three days of lanterns strung across every street between the Bowl and the harbour.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/ryu.alt: Ryu Ha-joon, Goldcrest Guild’s S-rank raid captain and the face of its broadcast, who called tonight’s gate clear two hours early

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/the_system.alt: The System, The voice in square brackets that only you can see, which has just offered you a hidden class

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_the_bowl.alt: The Bowl: Merrowgate’s great arena: a floor of raked sand, thirty thousand seats packed to the rails, and a bronze bell on a post at the edge of the sand.

story_cleanup_crew_e_rank/cover.alt: Cover art for Cleanup Crew, E-Rank: E-rank cleaner. Six hours. Hidden class.

story_struck_from_the_register/key.alt: Key art for Struck From the Register

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_reg.alt: The Register Hall: The ancestral hall of House Seol: dark beams, paper screens, forty kneeling cushions, and thirty-one generations of names in one folding book on a lacquer stand.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_old.alt: The Old Woodshed: A leaning shed at the back of the compound, split wood stacked to the roof and two posts scarred at chest height.

story_cut_loose_at_floor_99/cover.alt: Cover art for Cut Loose at Floor 99: They cut your rope. The dark caught you.

story_the_maid_owns_the_house_now/cover.alt: Cover art for The Maid Owns the House Now: She was your maid. Now you work for her.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_seo.alt: The Training Yard: Raked sand, forty disciples in house white, two lantern posts with their cords cut short, and a veranda where the Grandmaster watches the dawn forms.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_whe.alt: The Whetstone Room: A low room off the armoury that smells of oil and wet stone.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_tanners_ro.alt: Tanner’s Row: A steep lane of tanneries and rope-walks in the Lower Wards, smelling of lime and tar.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_the_harbou.alt: Merrowgate Harbour: Stone quays, cranes, bonded warehouses and a forest of masts.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_the_lamp.alt: The Lamp in the Wall: Your shrine: a niche the size of a bread oven in the wall at the bend of Tanner’s Row, a dented tin lamp inside it, and a century of soot above.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_twelve_bel.alt: The Twelve Bells: A loud tavern by the Bowl’s gate where champions drink after bouts and bookmakers chalk the odds over the bar.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_pon.alt: The Pond Pavilion: The Grandmaster’s tea pavilion over the carp pond: four pillars, a low table, a kettle always on, and the house ledger in a lacquer box.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_night_bake.alt: The Night Bakery: A narrow bakery in the Lower Wards that works from midnight to dawn.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_sea.alt: The Sealed Archive: A stone room under the register hall, reached by a ladder through the iron trapdoor.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Outer Kitchen: Three stoves, a rice pot big enough to sit in, and Old Cook Pyo, who has run this kitchen for twenty years and feeds the whole outer yard twice a day.
The Long Room: Twelve sleeping mats on a raised wooden floor, twelve boxes and one window that does not shut.
Key art for The Cult Master Wakes as a Servant

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_geu.alt: House Geum: House Geum, across the Long Bridge: gold lacquer gates, a yard laid with river stones, and disciples practising the second cut from open books on stands.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_swo.alt: Sword Street: The avenue of the seven sword houses: gates in seven colours, smithies, sharpening stalls, a teahouse where heirs pretend not to watch each other, and a gambling end where they do.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Outer Yard: A packed-earth yard behind the Silver Pine kitchens: a stone well, a woodshed with wet straw on its floor, washing lines, and sixty servants who start work before dawn.
The Training Court: A wide flagstone court ringed by old pines, where four hundred disciples run the morning forms in rows while servants stand at the edges holding target posts and towels.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_rol.alt: The Roll Office: A narrow city office with a long counter, a wall of pigeonholes, and the roll of every person allowed to carry a blade inside the walls.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_hearth_tem.alt: The Temple of All Gods: A round temple at the top of the city with a fire in a stone basin at its centre: the Hearth, which has never gone out.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_stenn_hous.alt: Stenn House: The Duke’s townhouse in the old quarter: grand, half-shuttered, the furniture under sheets in every room but two.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_the.alt: Under the Long Bridge: Under the Long Bridge after dark: rope rings strung between the pilings, lanterns on hooks, odds chalked on slates, and a crowd that does not ask names.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_golden_hou.alt: The Golden House: Lady Fortune’s temple on the hill: gold leaf on everything, a hall of offering bowls heaped with coins, priests in cream and gold.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Hall of Pines: The sect’s great hall: cedar beams, an altar at the far end, and a floor polished by a century of kneeling.

story_one_miracle_a_day/stage_the_cinder.alt: The Cinder Yard: A walled yard behind the Temple of All Gods where the clerks dump the shrines of gods who went out: cracked lamps, melted candles, soot-black statues, all heaped in drifts of old ash.

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_fer.alt: The Ferry Inn: Cheap rooms on stilts over the water, a common room with a fire, and a landlady who has seen a struck name walk in with nothing before.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Medicine Pavilion: The First Elder’s pavilion: drying racks of herbs, a wall of small labelled drawers, a brazier that is always warm, and on the desk a dispensary book in which every measure that leaves the room is written down in a neat hand.

story_one_miracle_a_day/tamsin.alt: Tamsin Reed, Your one follower. A dock porter fighting in the Hearth Games under your mark, with a borrowed sword

story_struck_from_the_register/stage_bou.alt: The Bout Ground: The island in the river where the Spring Bout is fought: one ring of raked sand, stands for four thousand, seven house banners, and a judges’ table for the Sword Council.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Cold Pool: A waterfall on the back mountain, a deep black pool beneath it, and a flat rock where disciples sit in the spray to train their breathing.
The Guest Pavilion: A quiet pavilion across a stone bridge from the Hall of Pines, swept and aired for the cult delegation.

story_struck_from_the_register/siwon.alt: Seol Siwon, Your younger sister, the best first-cut sword of your generation, and the heir the moment she cuts

story_struck_from_the_register/yeon.alt: Geum Yeon, Heir of House Geum, across the river, and the official witness at your striking

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Mountain Gate: A painted gate at the top of six hundred stone steps down to the road, and two bored gate disciples who check the tag of every servant going down to the village.

story_one_miracle_a_day/fortune.alt: Lady Fortune, The biggest god in Merrowgate, holder of the Hearth five years running, who sits at the gold rail and has noticed you

story_one_miracle_a_day/duke.alt: Duke Halvard Stenn, The Iron Duke. Five-time champion of the Hearth Games under Lady Fortune’s mark, and Tamsin’s first-round opponent

story_struck_from_the_register/jae.alt: Grandmaster Seol Jae, Head of House Seol and your grandfather, who ordered the striking

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: The Shrine on the Old Road: A roofless mountain shrine two hours up the old north road where nobody has prayed in years.

story_one_miracle_a_day/ash.alt: Brother Ash, Arbiter of the Hearth Games. A monk who prays to no god, and the only mortal in the arena who can see the Gallery

story_one_miracle_a_day/wick.alt: Wick, God of candle-ends, the last inch of every candle in the city. Your neighbour in the back row, down to one follower like you

story_struck_from_the_register/han.alt: Han, The old servant who keeps the house’s whetstones, and still calls you young master

story_one_miracle_a_day/sabine.alt: Mother Sabine Orlo, High Priestess of the Golden House, Lady Fortune’s temple. Keeps its books, holds its debts, and has challenged your right to be in the Games

story_struck_from_the_register/cover.alt: Cover art for Struck From the Register: Failed heir. Your sister holds the blade.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: Pinefoot Village: A market village at the foot of the mountain that lives off the sect: rice sellers, a blacksmith, an inn with a back room, and a noodle stall whose owner sells gossip along with the noodles.

The Camp at Grey Ford: A river crossing four hours east of the village where the cult delegation is camped for two nights before going up the mountain: nine tents, one cookfire, and nine riders who would know the Gravekeeper’s walk anywhere.

story_struck_from_the_register/doha.alt: Seol Doha, Your cousin, the best at the forms in the house, who wanted to be heir and never will be

story_struck_from_the_register/minseo.alt: Oh Minseo, Clerk of the Roll Office, who keeps the city’s roll of blades and rings the sundown bell

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: Baek Seo-ah, The sect leader’s daughter, the best sword of her generation at Silver Pine, and sworn since her mother’s funeral to kill the Gravekeeper

story_one_miracle_a_day/cover.alt: Cover art for One Miracle a Day: You’re a god. Only she still prays to you.

story_the_cult_master_wakes_as_a_servant.alt: Mok Gyeong-ho, Senior Disciple of Silver Pine, second-best sword of his generation, and the man who beat Dol in the woodshed last night
Pyo Man-deok, Head cook of the outer kitchen, who fed Dol for years and is the first person on the mountain to notice Dol is gone
Baek Mu-jin, Sect Leader of Silver Pine, Seo-ah’s father, and the man staking thirty years of funerals on one truce
Yu Seol-hwa, Your right hand for fifteen years, the woman who poured the wine, and now Acting Master of the Nine Graves, riding in to sign a truce
Gong Tae-seok, First Elder of Silver Pine, master of its Medicine Pavilion, and the gentlest voice on the mountain
Cover art for The Cult Master Wakes as a Servant: You died a legend. You woke up a servant.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_common_room.alt: The Third-Floor Common Room: A long room at the end of the third-floor corridor: a table nobody eats at properly, a television that only gets the weather, a noticeboard of floor rules in six different handwritings, and one plastic chair at the head of the table that nobody but Daigo sits in.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_room_307.alt: Room 307: Two bunks, two desks, one window that sticks, and a roommate’s half of the room already full of engine parts and snack wrappers.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_fourth_floo.alt: The Fourth Floor: The same corridor as the third, only cleaner and quieter, with blue-striped towels drying on every door handle and a desk chair at the top of the stairs where somebody is always sitting.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_back_stairs.alt: The Back Stairs: A concrete stairwell at the back of the building that smells of rust and floor polish.

story_noodles_or_blood/key.alt: Key art for Noodles or Blood

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_h.alt: The Old Man’s House: A wooden house at the top of the hill, nine minutes’ climb from the temple, with a garden gone to weeds and a study full of fishing-supply calendars.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_t.alt: The Temple Yard: Gravel, a stone lantern, an unused bin and a line of black cars, Kagami’s parked nose-out.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_the_roof.alt: The Roof: Water tanks, laundry lines, a broken plastic chair, and the whole port spread out below: cranes, container stacks, the canal, and the lit windows of the college workshops across the road.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_f.alt: The Funeral Hall: A rented hall behind a hillside temple, heavy with incense.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/key.alt: Key art for Inherited: One Failing Clan

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_h.alt: The Night Market: The old harbour ward’s night market: forty stalls under strings of bulbs, grilled squid, a bakery, a bathhouse chimney.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_lobby.alt: The Lobby: Mailboxes, a vending machine that keeps coins, a noticeboard where the housing office pins things nobody wants to read, and the warden’s window with a curfew clock behind it.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_warden_offi.alt: The Warden’s Office: A small office behind the lobby window, with a kettle, a radio tuned to the shipping forecast, a board of hooks with every spare key in the building on it, and a thick cloth-covered ledger open on the desk.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_dorm_kitche.alt: The Ground-Floor Kitchen: Six burners, of which four work, two rice cookers, a fridge with every shelf labelled by floor, and Ken’s corner, where the good knives are and nobody else is allowed.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_dry_showers.alt: The Dry Showers: A shower block shut for repairs two years ago and never repaired.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_boiler.alt: The Boiler Room: Coach Dam’s gym in the basement under the Annex, built around a boiler that bangs every forty minutes.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_tower.alt: The Tower: The ranked dorm: ten floors of glass and pale stone, ten fighters to a floor by number, with a card gate in the lobby, a gym that smells of new rubber and a physio on call.

story_the_ranking_board/key.alt: Key art for The Ranking Board

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_f.alt: The Family Office: One room up the back stairs from the noodle shop.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_p.alt: Pier 9: The last working pier in the old harbour, at the end of the market street.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_annex.alt: The Annex: The unranked dorm: six floors of 1970s concrete with a lift that works on Tuesdays.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_canal_lane.alt: The Canal Lane: A strip of cracked pavement between East Hall and the canal, lit by one streetlamp and by Ken’s noodle cart under the bridge from half past eleven.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_b.alt: The Breakwater: A concrete arm out into the bay from the end of Pier 9, with a small lighthouse at the tip and the glass tower on the new side lit up across the water.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_n.alt: Hachi’s Noodle Shop: A narrow noodle shop two doors from the market, its shutter permanently half down.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_l.alt: The Lantern: A tiny bar on the market corner, neutral ground under the harbour code for sixty years.

story_noodles_or_blood/daigo.alt: Daigo Hatanaka, Head of the third floor for three years, a final-year welding student, and the man who set your rent

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_yard.alt: The Yard: The stone courtyard at the centre of the college.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_scrapyard.alt: The Yard Under the Overpass: A scrap dealer’s yard under the motorway overpass: chain-link, floodlights, a dog that does not bark, and a portable cabin with a ledger in it.

story_noodles_or_blood/stage_workshops.alt: The College Workshops: A long brick block across the road: the welding bay, the engine shop, the electrical lab, the training kitchen, and the tool room in the middle, where every tool is signed in and out on a form by a student assistant with very neat handwriting.

story_noodles_or_blood/rumi.alt: Rumi Ogata, Electrical student, twenty, in her second year at the college, living in 309, and the only person on the third floor who has never paid the rent

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_tenth_.alt: The Tenth Floor: The top-ten dining room at the top of the Tower, where one table twenty feet long has become the Long Table.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_pit.alt: The Pit: A sunken stone arena behind the main hall, twelve tiers of seats around a white circle twice the size of the one in the Yard.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_h.alt: The Harbour Police Station: The harbour precinct station, up the block from the market: a front desk, a vending machine that only sells canned coffee, and the organised-crime desk upstairs, which is Detective Nori and a filing cabinet.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_tower_.alt: The Tower Roof: Laundry lines, two air vents, and the whole of Garam Bay laid out below to the cranes.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/stage_k.alt: The Kagami Tower: A glass tower on reclaimed land across the bridge, eighteen floors.

story_noodles_or_blood/cover.alt: Cover art for Noodles or Blood: Pay the floor in noodles, or in bruises.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_procto.alt: The Proctors’ Office: A long low room under the board, humming with the servers that run the glass.

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_ice_ro.alt: The Ice Room: The college clinic’s treatment floor: four ice baths, six tables, a wall of tape and a locked filing room at the back with Dr.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/ryo.alt: Ryo Okumura, The old man’s first lieutenant for sixteen years, who expected the seal to be his

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/saeko.alt: Saeko Imai, The family’s accountant, a former bank auditor, who knows what it is actually worth

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/kagami.alt: Tatsuo Kagami, Boss of the Kagami Group across the bay, your grandfather’s rival for forty years, and the man holding the note

story_noodles_or_blood/ken.alt: Ken Ueda, Final-year culinary student, keeper of the ground-floor kitchen and the late-night noodle cart, and the man who actually cooks the rent

story_noodles_or_blood/mabuchi.alt: Sota Mabuchi, Head of the fourth floor, a final-year machining student, and the student assistant in the workshop tool room

story_finals_week_outbreak/key.alt: Key art for Finals Week Outbreak

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_stairwe.alt: The Main Stairwell: Concrete stairs from the basement to the fourth floor, glass fire doors on every landing that sigh when they close, an extinguisher on every bracket.

story_noodles_or_blood/bunta.alt: Bunta Iwai, Auto mechanics student, nineteen, new to the college this year, and your roommate in 307, who paid his rent in noodles on day one and has been broke ever since

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_steps.alt: The Ninety-Nine Steps: Stone stairs from the college gate down the hill to the city.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_reading.alt: The Reading Room: The third-floor silent study room: forty metres of long oak tables, green lamps all switched off, tall arched windows over the quad.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_study_r.alt: The Study Rooms: Six glass-walled group rooms along the east side of the third floor.

story_noodles_or_blood/fujii.alt: Setsuko Fujii, Warden of East Hall for fourteen years, a former ship’s engineer, and the keeper of the incident book

story_the_ranking_board/stage_the_night_.alt: The Night Market: The street at the bottom of the steps: food stalls under strung bulbs, the Hamada fish stall with its awning half torn, a noodle place with nine stools that closes at two, and a flat above it where the clinic intern lives.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_the_sta.alt: The Stacks: Rows of steel shelving running into the dark, carrels along the windows, and a returns cart abandoned halfway down Architecture.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/cover.alt: Cover art for Inherited: One Failing Clan: Nine members. Ten million. Due tonight.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/mariko.alt: Mariko Kagami, Kagami’s daughter and heir, who runs his security firm and grew up on the same waterfront you are about to lose

story_the_ranking_board/stage_pier_six.alt: Pier Six: A disused cargo pier where people fight for cash in a ring of shipping pallets and car headlights.

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/nori.alt: Asako Nori, Organised-crime detective for the harbour precinct, who traded information with your grandfather for nineteen years

story_inherited_one_failing_clan/hachi.alt: Hachiro Ueda, Third lieutenant, the old man’s driver for twenty-six years, and the family’s cook

story_the_ranking_board/soyeon.alt: Soyeon Ryu, Number one on the board for 412 days. Third-year, 21, and the most watched person at the college

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_refe.alt: The Refectory: A long dining hall with a high table for the top of the Board and benches for everybody else.

story_the_ranking_board/tetsu.alt: Tetsu Hamada, Number 87. Fourth-year, 22, two discipline strikes, and stale at six tomorrow unless he defends today

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_colo.alt: The Colonnade: A long covered walkway of pale stone columns that joins every building on the hill.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_lobby.alt: The Lobby: The ground floor: a curved front desk, security gates, and a two-storey wall of glass onto the quad with hands pressed flat against the outside of it.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/key.alt: Key art for Ten Points to Expulsion

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_scho.alt: The Attic Corridor: The top floor of the oldest dormitory, under the roof, where the rooms cost nothing because the heating costs five points a week.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_exam.alt: The Examination Hall: Two hundred and twelve single desks in rows under a vaulted ceiling, a clock that ticks loudly enough to count by, and a raised dais at the front with a brass hand bell on it.

story_the_ranking_board/hajun.alt: Hajun Seol, Number 2. Fourth-year, 23, runs the Long Table on the tenth floor and the college’s challenge stream

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_securit.alt: The Security Office: A windowless room behind the front desk: sixteen camera feeds on four monitors, a key cabinet, a rack of charging radios, a first-aid box on the wall and a mug that says WORLD’S OKAYEST GUARD.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_library.alt: The Library Roof: Flat, gravelled, ringed with air-handling units.

story_affection_97/stage_ladies_gallery.alt: The Ladies’ Gallery: The upper corridor where the Queen’s ladies sleep, two to a narrow room, with a shared dressing room that smells of curling irons and orange water.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_special.alt: Special Collections: The fourth floor’s climate-controlled rare-book room behind a steel door with a keypad the Regulars have not learned yet.

story_affection_97/stage_long_gallery.alt: The Long Gallery: A hundred paces of polished floor under four centuries of royal portraits, with tall windows down one side and a draught down the whole length of it.

story_affection_97/stage_music_room.alt: The Blue Music Room: A long room papered in faded blue, with tall windows onto the gardens, a piano nobody tunes, and in the corner a gilded harp under a dust sheet that nobody has played since the court harpist was sent away.

story_affection_97/stage_rose_ballroom.alt: The Rose Ballroom: The great ballroom, hung with pale roses for the betrothal season, two hundred candles in three chandeliers, a musicians’ gallery, and a dance floor long enough that a person at one end cannot read a face at the other.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_basemen.alt: The Basement Stacks: Rolling compact shelving that closes like a mouth if anybody turns the wheels, bound journals back to 1890, pipes along the ceiling, and on the north wall a grey hatch painted the same grey as the pipes.

story_the_ranking_board/nari.alt: Nari Hwang, Final-year sports-medicine student, 24, who runs the Ice Room most days

story_the_ranking_board/minho.alt: Minho Tak, Your roommate in Annex 4-12. Second-year, 19, unranked, and a walking database of every fight at the Ridge

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_steam_t.alt: The Steam Tunnel: A hot concrete passage under the quad, low enough to stoop in, lagged pipes on both walls and one line of caged bulbs, every third one dead.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_ledg.alt: The Vault: A cold white room under the library basement, humming, with racks of machines behind glass and a single terminal on a steel desk.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_science.alt: Haas’s Lab: Second floor of the science building: two benches, fume hoods, a whiteboard of dosing curves nobody wiped, and a laboratory refrigerator with a padlock and a sticky note on it.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_coun.alt: The Council Chamber: A round room at the top of the council wing, glass on three sides, with eleven chairs around a table and a white one at the head of it.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_libr.alt: The Harcourt Library: Three floors of oak and green lamps, paid for by Ren’s grandfather and named for him.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_port.alt: The Porter’s Lodge: A stone lodge in the arch of the main gate, a stove, a logbook, a key board and a stool by the fire that the night porter lets students sit on until a quarter past eleven.

story_affection_97/stage_moon_terrace.alt: The Moon Terrace: A stone terrace outside the ballroom’s glass doors, with a balustrade, steps down to the gardens, and the music coming through the doors half a bar late.

story_the_ranking_board/dam.alt: Coach Dam Gyeongsuk, Instructor, 58, two-time national open champion, who coaches only the unranked in the basement under the Annex

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_boat.alt: The Old Boathouse: A timber boathouse on the river at the foot of the hill, its boats long gone, a roped ring in the middle of the floor and a medic’s bench by the door.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_the_qua.alt: The Quad: Open lawns crossed by paths, benches, a stone fountain switched off.

story_affection_97/stage_ashgrove_suite.alt: The Ashgrove Suite: The best guest rooms in the palace, given to the bride: green silk walls, a writing desk covered in letters to a bank, more pearl combs than anybody needs, and a door with a lock on the inside that Lady Viola actually uses.

story_affection_97/stage_palace_gardens.alt: The Queen’s Gardens: Clipped box hedges, gravel walks, a rose maze that is easy to get lost in on purpose, and at the far end a high old brick wall with a locked iron door in it that the gardeners walk past without looking at.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_health_.alt: The Health Centre: Where it began.

story_affection_97/stage_sunken_garden.alt: The Sunken Garden: A walled garden nobody tends, four steps down from the level of the rest, overgrown with ivy and old roses.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_exam_ha.alt: The Exam Hall: Two hundred single desks in perfect rows, a candidate number on each, an invigilator’s clock on the stage, and double doors that lock from the outside.

story_affection_97/stage_queens_solar.alt: The Queen’s Solar: The Queen’s private study: a sunny upper room with a great desk, a tea table, shelves of household ledgers, and a fire lit in every season.

story_finals_week_outbreak/stage_main_ga.alt: The Main Gate: The campus entrance turned into a checkpoint: floodlights, two lines of tape, a white screening tent with a thermal camera at its mouth, and a loudhailer reading the rules every ten minutes.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_brac.alt: Brack Street: The one street of the town at the foot of the hill: a cafe that takes money instead of points, a launderette, a bus stop with a night bus, and the office of the town newspaper.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/yui.alt: Yui Arakawa, Your friend across the attic hall, first-year on a bursary, and three points from being sent home

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/stage_prov.alt: The Provost’s House: A tall grey house at the far side of the lawn, with a polished door, a drawing room where tea is served to students who are about to be told something, and a study at the back with a terminal in it that answers to one brass key.

story_finals_week_outbreak/nora.alt: Nora Lindqvist, Fourth-year medical student, sharing your table since midnight, and the only person here who has watched somebody turn

story_finals_week_outbreak/kwame.alt: Kwame Mensah, Night security officer, six years on this building, master keys on his belt and the county on his radio

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/ren.alt: Ren Harcourt, Student president, fourth-year, and the richest balance on the Board

story_affection_97/stage_map_library.alt: The Map Library: A two-storey room of maps and ledgers of the kingdom, a long map table under hanging lamps, and a spiral stair up to the prince’s private rooms.

story_finals_week_outbreak/cover.alt: Cover art for Finals Week Outbreak: They learned door handles tonight.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/grey.alt: Tobias Grey, Proctor of examinations and night porter at the gate. Staff, so the Ledger does not score him

story_affection_97/stage_tiltyard.alt: The Tiltyard: A sanded yard behind the stables where the palace guard drills, with the guard barracks along one side, a rack of blunted practice swords, and Sir Bastien most mornings, winning.

story_affection_97/stage_palace_chapel.alt: The Rose Chapel: A small white chapel with a rose window, where every royal betrothal for three hundred years has been sealed in front of the court.

story_finals_week_outbreak/declan.alt: Declan Shaw, Second-year law student barricaded in a study room with a whiteboard over the glass and a rule for everything

story_finals_week_outbreak/lily.alt: Lily Tran, First-year architecture student who has drawn every floor of this building, and has not slept in sixty hours

story_affection_97/stage_postern_gate.alt: The Postern Gate: A small iron gate in the outer wall behind the stables, with one bored guard, one lantern, and a lane down the hill into the lower town.

story_finals_week_outbreak/haas.alt: Professor Konrad Haas, Professor of pharmacology, locked in Special Collections with a grey binder he will not put down, and the man the helicopter is coming for

story_affection_97/stage_lantern_street.alt: Lantern Street: A crooked street in the lower town, a mile from the palace, with a chandler’s shop, an inn with music most nights, and up a flight of outside stairs a rented room with a tall harp in it where Maren Lisle teaches anyone who pays.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/margot.alt: Margot Ashdown, Council treasurer, third-year, who keeps the books and enjoys it

story_affection_97/aldric.alt: Crown Prince Aldric, The crown prince, who says he despises you, and over whose head a number says otherwise

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/bastian.alt: Bastian Kroll, Fourth-year who runs the ring in the old boathouse, and Ren’s oldest friend

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/cover.alt: Cover art for Ten Points to Expulsion: Ten points left, and a bribe to fail.

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/marsh.alt: Honora Marsh, Provost of Tallis College, who wears the only key to the Ledger on a ribbon at her neck

story_ten_points_to_expulsion/ledger.alt: The Ledger, The college’s scoring system. It sees through every band and lens on campus and adds or takes away points by the Tariff

story_affection_97/viola.alt: Lady Viola Ashgrove, The crown prince’s intended bride, whom you attend this fortnight, and who has her own plan

story_affection_97/bastien.alt: Sir Bastien Roche, The prince’s sworn knight and oldest friend, who flirts with you in public and has no number over his head

story_the_ranking_board/cover.alt: Cover art for The Ranking Board: A hundred names. Yours is not one yet.

story_affection_97/cress.alt: Lady Cressida Fane, Senior lady-in-waiting, your roommate and friend, and the Queen’s ears among her ladies

story_affection_97/maren.alt: Maren Lisle, The court harpist dismissed two springs ago for a theft, and the only person the prince still writes to

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_your_roo.alt: Your Room: A narrow bedroom at the back of the house on Ferry Road, exactly as you left it ten years ago: posters you are embarrassed by, a desk with a drawer that sticks, a graduation gown on the back of the door, and a soft blue window over the bed that is not part of the house.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_gara.alt: Dad’s Garage: Two bays, a hydraulic lift that works if you kick it, a radio tuned to the same station for twenty years, and an office whose desk drawer is full of letters from the bank.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_ferry_ro.alt: Ferry Road: The street you grew up on, running downhill to the lake: eleven houses, the garage at the bottom, the Dela Cruz porch two doors down with a basketball hoop nobody has used in years, and the old ferry pier at the very end where the road gives up.

story_restart_at_eighteen/key.alt: Key art for Restart at Eighteen

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_your_hou.alt: The House on Ferry Road: A two-bedroom house with a kitchen that smells of coffee and engine oil, a fridge covered in ten years of takeaway menus, and a kitchen drawer Dad has started keeping closed.

story_affection_97/ottilie.alt: Queen Ottilie, Queen Regent and your employer, who had a harpist sent away for being liked, and would do it again

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_bake.alt: The Bakery: The Lindgren family bakery: a bell over the door, the last trays of the day going cheap, and a staircase at the back up to the flat where Sara has lived her whole life.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_hardware.alt: Ashcroft Hardware: The biggest shop in town, with Graham Ashcroft’s office above it.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_bus_shel.alt: The Bus Shelter: A glass shelter at the end of Main Street with one bench, one bin, and a timetable that has not changed in ten years.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_main_str.alt: Main Street: Four blocks of town: the bakery, Ashcroft Hardware, a pharmacy, a pizza place with three tables, and the bus shelter at the far end with a timetable everybody knows by heart.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_lake.alt: The Lake House: The Ashcroft summer house on the north shore: a deck bigger than your whole house, string lights, a bonfire on the lawn, a speaker system loud enough to reach the far bank, and ninety people from your class in various states of sunburn.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_boat.alt: The Boathouse: A two-storey wooden boathouse with a flat tar roof you can climb onto from the railing, and a boat shed beside it full of fuel cans, life jackets and a sailing dinghy nobody has taken out in years.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_stud.alt: Graham’s Study: A wood-panelled room off the side of the lake house with a desk, two leather chairs, a framed map of the waterfront with half the lots shaded in, and a window onto the lawn where you can see the whole party without hearing it.

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_old_pier.alt: The Old Pier: The ferry stopped running before you were born and nobody ever took the pier down.

story_restart_at_eighteen/sara.alt: Sara Lindgren, The one you lost. Top of the class, gave the graduation speech this morning, and leaves town on the 6:10 bus tomorrow

story_restart_at_eighteen/stage_the_save.alt: The Save Room: Inside the window.

story_affection_97/cover.alt: Cover art for Affection: 97: He says he despises you. It says 97.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_ticke.alt: The Ticket Counter: Your counter: a long oak booking desk behind a brass grille at the head of the concourse, with a bell, an ink pad and Ida’s chair still warm.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_lamp_.alt: The Lamp Room: At the top of ninety-nine iron stairs from the concourse, a round glass room over the whole station.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/key.alt: Key art for The Zombie Who Said Please

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_l.alt: Kestrel Lock: A long island between the canal and the river, with the lock chamber down the middle, two narrowboats tied up, a cook fire under a tarpaulin and washing on a line.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_the_c.alt: The Concourse: A vast iron-and-glass hall with nine platforms fanned out from it, each under its own coloured lamp, and a station clock over the board that stopped at midnight.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_lost_.alt: Lost Property: A long room off the concourse, shelved to the roof with everything ever left on a train through Lantern Cross: umbrellas from a thousand worlds, a stuffed bear the size of a door, a jar of keys that sing when it is opened.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: The Lock-Keeper’s Cottage: Cole’s office at the front, with a desk, a radio and a shelf of ledgers; the camp kitchen at the back, with the only proper stove on the island and a kettle that is always on.

story_every_platform_a_world/key.alt: Key art for Every Platform a World

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: The Pump House: A cold brick room with a dead beam engine taking up most of it, one high barred window, and a door that bolts from the outside.
The Wire: The landward fence of Kestrel Lock: chain-link and pallets strung with tin cans, a scaffold watchtower, and a single mesh gate onto a footbridge that winches up at night.

story_restart_at_eighteen/dad.alt: Dad, Your father. Tomas to everybody else on Ferry Road. Runs a two-bay garage with one employee, who is him

story_restart_at_eighteen/jun.alt: Jun Dela Cruz, Your best friend for as long as either of you can remember. Lives two doors down, and is due at the fire service academy in August

story_restart_at_eighteen/theo.alt: Theo Ashcroft, Host of tonight’s party, Graham Ashcroft’s son, and the one who lights the crate at 10:40

story_restart_at_eighteen/graham.alt: Graham Ashcroft, Owns the hardware store, the marina and most of the waterfront. Buying Dad’s garage tonight at ten

story_restart_at_eighteen/cover.alt: Cover art for Restart at Eighteen: Ten years back. One night to fix it.

story_restart_at_eighteen/the_system.alt: The System, The window only you can see. It brought you back, and it will not say why

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_waiti.alt: The First-Class Waiting Room: Velvet benches, a coal fire, a brass samovar that is never empty, and heavy curtains for travellers who do not like daylight.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_condu.alt: The Conductor’s Carriage: The last carriage of a train that never leaves, on a siding at the far end of the concourse.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_platf.alt: Platform 4: A dark platform off the concourse under a lamp of cold vermilion glass.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_akebo.alt: The Road Below Castle Akebono: A riverside road at the foot of a castle on a hill, an hour before dawn.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: The Weir: Where the river drops over a concrete sill beside the island, loud and white.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_platf.alt: Platform 6: A dark platform off the concourse under a white lamp gone black.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_f.alt: The Ferry Landing: A stone landing below the weir where the Ferrymen tie up their barge: a long black hull with a wheelhouse, diesel drums on the deck, a striped awning and a brazier.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: Doc’s Boathouse: A boathouse turned into a clinic: two camp beds, a fridge that runs off the generator, a borrowed college microscope, and a whiteboard covered in Doc’s handwriting about you.
The Towpath: The canal path outside the wire, running north between hedges and black water.
The Radio Shed: A shed on stilts at the end of the island with a tall aerial lashed to it, a bench of radios in various states of repair, and a generator that thumps like a heart.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_apart.alt: Apartment 4C: The top flat, under the roof.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_s.alt: The Stairs: Five flights of worn stairs with a brass rail polished by a hundred years of hands.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_r.alt: The Roof: Tar and gravel, a dead water tank, two folding chairs nobody admits to owning, and the whole city lit up to the river.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/key.alt: Key art for Rent Is One True Story

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_dee_3.alt: Apartment 3B: Plants on every surface, a drinks trolley used entirely for tea, a sofa with a permanent dent, and a grey cat called Deposit who belongs to nobody and lives here.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_owl_m.alt: The Owl Market: A night bazaar twenty-five minutes from the concourse by the Platform 5 train, under strings of paper lamps.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_platf.alt: Platform 8: A dark platform off the concourse under a lamp of violet glass.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_long_.alt: The Bridge of the Long Patience: The bridge of a deep-space survey ship in a dead orbit: emergency red lighting, frost on the inside of the windows, six crew in thermal blankets taking slow breaths.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_moonw.alt: The Moonward Court: The throne hall of Ostravel, where it is always night: a floor of black glass, a ceiling open to an enormous moon, and the night nobility in silver and black.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_salt_.alt: The Salt Coast: A harbour town in another world, forty minutes from the concourse by the Platform 1 train.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: The North Road: The valley road out of the hills, lined with abandoned cars nose to tail under a motorway bridge.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_s.alt: St Ide’s Hospital: A seven-storey hospital on the hill above the town, every window dark, ambulances still parked at angles in the bay.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_t.alt: The Railway Cutting: A deep railway cutting nine miles north, walls of wet rock either side, filled from end to end with greys standing shoulder to shoulder and humming.
Holt’s Chemist: A narrow chemist’s shop under a blue sign, shelves half emptied two years ago and then left alone.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_w.alt: Wexley High Street: A dead market town a mile down the lane: shop fronts with the glass gone, a bus shelter, bunting still up from a summer fair two years ago.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/cover.alt: Cover art for The Zombie Who Said Please: You died. You kept your manners.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_apart.alt: Apartment 1A: Floor-to-ceiling newspapers in labelled bundles, a typesetter’s cabinet of tiny drawers, a radio that has been on since 1969, and an armchair placed to see everybody who comes in the street door.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_b.alt: The Basement: Below the boiler room, through a door that locks from the inside: one long cool room with a desk, a green lamp, a ledger, a wall of photographs older than the building, and a second door, heavy, with no keyhole at all.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_ashby.alt: Ashby Street: A narrow street of old walk-ups that has been about to be redeveloped since 1990.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/stage_w.alt: Ward Nine: The trial ward on the fourth floor: forty beds in two rows, curtains drawn back, a nurses’ station with files spilling out of the drawers.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_bridg.alt: The City of Bridges: A city with no ground, only towers rising out of fog and bridges strung between them, thirty minutes from the concourse by the Platform 3 train at a quarter past each hour.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_giant.alt: The Field of Sleeping Giants: A snowfield where giants the size of hills lie asleep under the drifts, thirty-five minutes from the concourse by the Platform 7 train, which runs every forty minutes.

story_every_platform_a_world/ren.alt: Ren Shiomi, Samurai of House Uraga, sent out of a besieged castle with his lord’s last order, and trying to get back in

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_l.alt: The Lobby: Black and white tiles, nine brass mailboxes with four names on them, a noticeboard, and a narrow door under the stairs with no handle on the outside.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_st_an.alt: St. Anselm’s: A brick church with a deep stone porch, a chessboard set up on the porch bench under a plastic cover, and a nave Elias will not walk into.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_glass.alt: The Glass Desert: Dunes of green glass under a white moon, twenty minutes from the concourse by the Platform 2 train, which runs at twenty past each hour.

story_every_platform_a_world/stage_one_t.alt: The Forest of One Tree: A forest that is a single living tree, its branches and roots running for miles, twenty-five minutes from the concourse by the Platform 9 train at ten to each hour.

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/doc.alt: Ife Amari, The camp’s doctor, who was a vet before the grey, and who has wanted a subject like you for two years

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/sunny.alt: Sunny Abara, Runs the generator and the radios, and decided inside a minute that you are the best thing to happen at the Lock in two years

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/cole.alt: Cole Garrity, The man who runs Kestrel Lock by arithmetic, and the man on the watchtower who told Jessa to shoot

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/jessa.alt: Jessa Marlow, Night watch on the wire, the best shot at Kestrel Lock, and the only person who has not pulled the trigger

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/ivo.alt: Ivo Kade, Captain of the Ferrymen, a river trader who buys anything rare, and who has come up the weir to buy you

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_l.alt: The All-Night Laundromat: Twenty machines, three of which work properly, a folding table, a vending machine that only sells soup, and fluorescent light at four in the morning.

story_every_platform_a_world/conductor.alt: The Conductor, Runs every train through Lantern Cross, answers exactly the question asked, and cannot climb the stairs to the lamp

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_recor.alt: The Records Office: The city treasurer’s counter on the second floor of an annex downtown: numbered tickets, a long queue, a clerk who has seen every trick, and the auction room next door where Lot 14 will be sold at ten on the tenth.

story_every_platform_a_world/cover.alt: Cover art for Every Platform a World: Three travellers, one ticket, your call.

story_every_platform_a_world/okafor.alt: Commander Adaeze Okafor, Commander of the survey ship Long Patience, whose crew is breathing reserve air in a dead orbit on the far side of Platform 6

story_every_platform_a_world/isolde.alt: Queen Isolde, Queen of Ostravel, a kingdom where it is always night, stranded behind Platform 8 on the night her cousin is to be crowned

story_rent_is_one_true_story/elias.alt: Elias Varga, Your landlord. Collects the rent at midnight on the first, in person, from the landing side of your door

story_rent_is_one_true_story/stage_the_o.alt: The Orchid Room: A late bar across town behind an unmarked green door: velvet booths, a piano nobody plays before two, and a back booth that is always reserved.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/celine.alt: Celine Marchand, The vampire who made Elias, and his ex. Runs a late bar across town and has come back for him

story_the_zombie_who_said_please/the_hor.alt: The Horde, About four thousand greys walking down the valley as one crowd, and the only voice in the world that sounds like home to you

story_every_platform_a_world/ida.alt: Ida Fennimore, Night stationmaster of Lantern Cross for forty-one years, retired at sunset tonight to a room over a fish restaurant on the Salt Coast

story_rent_is_one_true_story/cover.alt: Cover art for Rent Is One True Story: He doesn’t want money. He wants the truth.

story_rent_is_one_true_story/gus.alt: Gus Bellweather, The oldest tenant. Ground floor, 1A, since 1969. A retired newspaper typesetter

story_rent_is_one_true_story/dee.alt: Dee Moss, Your neighbour in 3B. Runs the all-night laundromat on the corner, and posted the ad for your flat

story_rent_is_one_true_story/tom.alt: Father Tom Kowalski, The priest at St. Anselm’s across the street, and Elias’s chess partner for twenty years

story_three_feet_apart/stage_long_galler.alt: The Long Gallery: The spine of the palace: three hundred feet of portraits of every archmage since the founding, tall windows on one side, doors on the other, and courtiers who stop talking when you pass.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_lantern_hal.alt: The Lantern Hall: The court’s great hall: a hundred hanging lanterns, the Queen’s high table on a dais, and in the middle of the floor the iron brazier where the court burns its disputation questions.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_west_tower.alt: His Tower: Caius Wren’s rooms in the West Tower, up three hundred and twelve stairs on a spiral built for one: bare boards, ward lines chalked on every threshold, one hard chair, one very tidy bed, and on the mantel a silver inkwell that is technically yours.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_east_tower.alt: Your Tower: Your rooms at the top of the East Tower: a workroom with every surface covered, a narrow bed under a slanted window, a window seat, and a door to the antechamber where your apprentice sleeps on a cot.

story_three_feet_apart/key.alt: Key art for Three Feet Apart

story_three_feet_apart/stage_treaty_vaul.alt: The Treaty Vault: A cold stone room under the library where the war treaties are kept rolled in lead tubes.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_royal_libra.alt: The Royal Library: Four floors of shelves around a well of light, a librarian who has taken a vow of quiet and enforces it on everybody else, and at the very back a bronze door to the treaty vault that will not open for somebody who does not know what they are looking for.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_archmage_st.alt: The Archmage’s Study: The top of the Old Tower: a round room of books and teapots, a desk the size of a cart, and a locked cabinet behind it.

story_three_feet_apart/stage_chancery.alt: The Chancery: The Chancellor’s offices: a clerks’ room full of scratching pens, a Seal Room with the Queen’s great seal on a velvet cushion, and Corvina’s own desk, very clean, with a fresh blotting sheet that is not quite fresh enough.

story_three_feet_apart/cover.alt: Cover art for Three Feet Apart: Bound to your rival. Three feet, no more.
